### Step 4.2b — Compute worker core (`src/workers/compute`) (2026-09-30)

**Done.** The replica, its handlers, the main-thread sync, the method specs, tests at every level, a bench. No new dependency, no schema change. `adoptPending` is NOT here (moved to 4.2c, step 4.2a review); the import, export and snapshot methods keep their old shape and answer `NOT_READY` as a value until 4.2c.

- **Replica** (`replica.ts`, pure and synchronous). `load(state, revision)` builds the full index engine, runs `validateAll`, fills its own `FindingStore`, and answers `PrecomputedFindings` (findings, `RULE_SET_ID`, revision, record counts): exactly what `replaceState` and `reload` take. A refused load (`BAD_REQUEST`: bad revision, missing tables) leaves the old replica untouched. `apply(changes)` follows the store's commit step: Immer patches, the index engine's `apply`, `validateTouchedByRule(next, indexes, touched, previous, replica.findings)`; `previous` is never omitted. The revision rule is the core index engine's (one step ahead; a `'remote'` ChangeSet any forward span); otherwise the VALUE `{ ok: false, code: 'REPLICA_STALE', have }` and nothing changes. A ChangeSet whose patches cannot be applied throws (`INTERNAL`), leaves state and revision as they were and rebuilds the consumed index handle. `validateAll(revision)` and `findRoutes(revision, query)` answer the same refusal for another revision; before the first load every call is `NOT_READY`. `findRoutes` times its budget with the injected `nowMs` (no `Date.now`); the call's abort signal replaces `query.limits.signal`.
- **Contract change** (`src/workers/rpc/contracts.ts`, see Amendments): `loadReplica` answers `PrecomputedFindings`; `applyChanges`, `validateAll`, `findRoutes` answer `ReplicaAnswer<...>` (`{ ok: true, ... }` or `ReplicaStale`); `findRoutes` takes `{ revision, query }`; `WorkerEvent` gains `replica_status`. Specs (`specs.ts`): idempotent `loadReplica`, `validateAll`, `findRoutes`, `importPreview`, `buildExport`; NOT idempotent `applyChanges`. Timeouts as in ADR-034.
- **Host** (`handlers.ts`, `host.ts`, `entry.ts`): `startComputeHost(port, clock)` is the real host over the real handlers; `entry.ts` is the browser entry (creating the worker is Phase 5, D7).
- **Sync** (`sync.ts`, main thread). `createReplicaSync({ factory, store, ... })` builds the client itself (so `onRestart` can be wired), subscribes to the store, forwards every ChangeSet (commit, undo, redo, replace, remote) in order, one at a time. **Reloads instead of forwarding** (one `loadReplica` of the store's CURRENT state, the queue dropped) when the worker answers `REPLICA_STALE` or refuses in any other way (`INTERNAL`, `BAD_REQUEST`...), or when more than **100 ChangeSets or 2,000 touched records** are waiting (the bound, chosen from the bench below). After a crash or timeout the client restarts the worker and the `onRestart` hook loads the store's current state before any other call; the sync then waits for that hook instead of re-sending the apply (never retried), and drops queued ChangeSets already inside the loaded state. A hook that fails, or a worker that crashes during the hook, starts over (the client's own cap and hook timeout apply). Status: `status()` value (`state`, `reason`, `replicaRevision`, `storeRevision`, `queued`, `reloads`), `settled()`, and a `replica_status` WorkerEvent on every change of state (`reloading` at creation, `in_sync`, `down`). `down` = the client gave up (`gave_up`) or the worker refused a reload; the queue is dropped, the store subscription ends, and later commits are not an error.
- **Tests** (+40: 168 files / 2,728 tests -> 172 / 2,768). `replica.test.ts` 16, `sync.test.ts` 15 (in memory; every message cloned), `tests/property/replica.test.ts` 5 (P-07 style: replica == store (state, revision, every index answer, findings vs the store AND vs `validateAll`) after random command sequences with undo, redo and a replaceState, plus a non-vacuity test that all four causes are reached; P-11 style on the ADV-012 and like-water hub shapes with the same raw-recipe edits as `validation-scope.test.ts`, moved to `src/test-support/scope-edits.ts` without changing any assertion; the findings `loadReplica` answers accepted by `replaceState` and `reload` with `verifyPrecomputed` on, the ERROR gate behaving as in process), `tests/integration/compute-worker-threads.test.ts` 3 (a real `worker_threads` thread running the real compute host under tsx: follows the store; an induced crash under `validateAll` (the thread exits when that request arrives, via a port wrapper in the fixture only) restarts, reloads and retries once; an induced crash under `applyChanges` reloads and does not repeat the apply), `tests/types` +1. "Previous never omitted": a spy validator records `previous` for commit, undo, redo, replace and remote ChangeSets (all `validateTouchedByRule`, all defined, `validateTouched` and `scopeOf` never called) with a negative control. Every param and result passes `structuredClone` (the in-memory port clones every message; the replica tests clone explicitly too). Five hand mutants (skip rule removed, `previous` dropped, no wait after a crash, off-by-one bound, remote span refused) were each killed. `npm run check` as ONE command at the default cap (4 workers): 172 files, 2,768 tests, Vitest 149 s (whole check 3 min 30 s).
- **Bench** (`tests/perf/compute-replica.bench.ts`, run once alone; informal; `budgets.mjs` entries added; not `bench:baseline`, not `bench:compare`), design tier, mean / p99 ms. Worker code (no thread): applyChanges ordinary edit 1.12 / 2.32; hub record edit (rename of the 1,000-referrer hub, ONE record touched, previous passed) 16.5 / 21.8; hub edit (`replaceReferences`, ~1,020 records touched) 448.4 / 465.6; `validateAll` dense 298.0 / 307.7 and hub_explosion 254.2 / 262.0 (budget row < 3 s: met by 10x); load (index build + validateAll) dense 831.3 / 850.7. Real thread: applyChanges round trip, ordinary edit 1.56 / 5.36; `loadReplica` of the whole design-tier state 1,308 / 1,327; the sender's blocking part of that clone (`v8.serialize`) 56.8 / 190.8. **Drift:** an earlier run of the same file the same session (also alone) read about 2.3x slower on every entry (ordinary 2.42 / 4.73, hub edit 1,044 / 1,085, validateAll 712 and 591, load 1,979, thread loadReplica 3,097, serialize 108.9); the backlog bound uses the range. A scratch breakdown of the hub edit (not committed): patches about 140 ms, part-1 index apply about 120 ms, full index apply about 420 ms, `validateTouchedByRule` about 300-460 ms. **D2 not measured:** the core indexes are class instances with private fields and Maps of a lineage, not plain data; reaching in would change a contract.
- **Not built.** `adoptPending` (4.2c); import, export, snapshot methods (4.2c, 4.2d); creating the sync and a status banner in the app (Phase 5); Q10 (b) (4.3b).
- **Amendments** (CLAUDE.md §7): see the Amendments list. Docs: ADR-034 bullet.

**REVIEW REQUIRED**
1. `findRoutes` takes `{ revision, query }` instead of a bare `RouteQuery` (the plan says "as they are", and also "refused when the revision asked is not the replica's"; a bare query has no revision). Results of `loadReplica`, `applyChanges`, `validateAll`, `findRoutes` changed as described above.
2. The replica keeps the FULL index engine (route search needs the cross-record indexes; the store keeps the part-1 engine). It makes a hub edit cost about 300 ms more in the worker. Alternative: maintain the part-1 indexes and build the full ones lazily per revision for `findRoutes`. Kept because it is simple and off the main thread; the hub edit is the rare case.
3. Backlog bounds: 100 ChangeSets AND 2,000 touched records, from the bench. The count alone would have been wrong (a hub edit is about 1,000 times an ordinary one).
4. A reload the worker refuses (not a crash) ends in `down`, not in a retry loop. `down` is final for a sync; how the app recovers or shows it is Phase 5.
5. `importPreview` and `buildExport` answer `NOT_READY` (a value) until 4.2c.
6. The real-thread tests start `startComputeHost`, the function the browser entry calls; `entry.ts` itself needs `self`. Only the port differs (and, for the induced crash, the fixture's port wrapper).
7. `in_sync` means "following": ChangeSets may still be queued (`queued`, `settled()` says when caught up).

### Step 4.2c — Import in the compute worker, snapshotBuild, the snapshot bytes entry point, adoptPending (2026-09-30)

**Done.** The import session runs in the compute worker; main's apply orchestrator drives it through ports; the persistence adapter has ONE bytes entry point; the replica adopts a pending state instead of receiving the merged state twice. No new dependency, no schema change. Export stays `NOT_READY` (moved to 4.2e, step 4.2b review). Everything a-e of the master prompt is built and tested; nothing was left over.

- **Worker import host** (`src/workers/compute/import-host.ts`, `ids.ts`). `importPreview({ source: Blob, fileName, request?, ids })`, `importRevise({ batchId, request, ids })`, `importCancel`, `importPrepareApply({ batchId, plan, baseRevision })`. The unchanged Phase 3 `createImportSession` runs over a store view of the REPLICA; one call at a time; the pending batch (at most one) lives in the worker. A revise or prepare against a replica that is not at the revision the preview was built on is a value (`STALE_REVISION`, batch consumed). The `IdFactory` is rebuilt per call from `{ nowIso, seed }` (`idFactoryFrom`, mulberry32; bad data is `BAD_REQUEST`); the worker has no clock or RNG of its own for IDs. Legacy files use the same session. The file crosses as a Blob (structured clone shares its bytes; a Blob cannot be in a transfer list), the asset buffers of `importPrepareApply` are transferred.
- **io** (`src/io/import-prepare.ts`, `import-apply.ts`, `import-session.ts`). `ImportSession.prepareApply(batchId, plan, liveRevision)` is the pure half of `apply` (UNKNOWN_BATCH, PLAN_MISMATCH, STALE_REVISION (consumes), BLOCKED; nothing written, batch stays pending), `consume`, `pendingBaseRevision`. The report split into `buildReportDraft` (everything but the time and the snapshot ID) + `completeReport`, `quarantineDraftsOf`, `storeImportReport`; `applyImport` uses them (Phase 3 tests unchanged and green). `ImportSessionDeps` write ports are optional: a session without them cannot `apply` (REJECTED as a value).
- **Replica pending state** (`replica.ts`): `prepare(state, revision)` (index build + `validateAll` once, keeps the result as PENDING, answers `PrecomputedFindings`), `adopt(revision)` (swap; refusals `NO_PENDING` / `PENDING_REVISION` / `REPLICA_STALE` as values), `drop()`, `pendingRevision()`. A load or an ordinary apply drops it.
- **snapshotBuild** (`snapshot-build.ts`): `snapshotBuild({ revision, reason, exportedAt })`, bytes of the replica, transferred; `REPLICA_STALE` as a value. A worker cannot import persistence, so the few lines of `buildSnapshot` are repeated here; a test proves byte equality with the codec.
- **The bytes entry point: `storeSnapshotBytes(input)`** on the persistence adapter (`SnapshotBytesInput { bytes, reason, revision, schemaVersion, note? }`, result `{ ok: true, summary } | { ok: false, code: 'STALE_REVISION' | 'BAD_BYTES', message, current? }`). Stores the bytes as they are in the write queue's order; `revision` must be the adapter's current revision (new `WriteQueue.currentRevision()`: the newest revision the queue was given). Bytes from `snapshotBuild` read back with `readSnapshot` and `restoreSnapshot` restores the same state (tests).
- **Apply orchestrator** (`src/workers/compute/import-flow.ts`, ports only): settle the sync, `importPrepareApply`, STALE check, `snapshotBuild('pre_import')`, `storeSnapshotBytes`, UNKNOWN_BATCH check (cancel or a newer preview while the snapshot was written), STALE check, `sync.expectAdoption(revision + 1)`, asset stage, ONE `store.replaceState(merged, 'import', precomputed)`, batch report and quarantine rows. Every failure deletes the snapshot (when stored), clears the expectation and sends `dropPending`; a store refusal changes nothing (Phase 3 behaviour). It answers the same `ImportApplyResult`. A worker crash on the prepare call is `UNKNOWN_BATCH`, on the snapshot call `SNAPSHOT_FAILED`; nothing changed either way.
- **Sync** (`sync.ts`): `expectAdoption(revision)` / `clearAdoption()`; on the `replace` ChangeSet at the announced revision it sends `adoptPending` instead of forwarding the ChangeSet (no second whole-state transfer); a refusal or failure makes it reload.

a refused adoption reloads). `compute-import-failures.test.ts` (23): INV-21 at every failure point (snapshot not stored, stale, damaged bytes, store refuses the findings, `replaceState` throws, a commit while the snapshot is stored, a cancel while it is stored, `snapshotBuild` fails, replica stale): live state (same reference), revision, history, stored snapshots, batch reports, persisted state and replica all as before, no pending state left; STALE_REVISION (apply and revise), cancel, PLAN_MISMATCH, BLOCKED, crash between preview and apply and under `snapshotBuild` (UNKNOWN_BATCH / nothing changed), structuredClone of every result, per-call IDs, parse refusals and CANCELLED as values, asset bytes transferred (detached in the worker; Worker code (no thread): `importPreview` parse -> preview total, dense into an EMPTY store 3,245.5 / 3,540.3 (row < 5 s: met), hub_explosion into a design-tier store with every ID conflicting 1,532.9 / 1,630.7 (met; the Gate E watch item: about 1.5 s, was 1.17 s in process in step 3.7, within run-to-run drift); `importPrepareApply` (the merged state's replica) 2,334.6 / 2,467.4 (dense) and 1,364.3 / 2,115.6 (hub_explosion, rme 55%); `snapshotBuild` 473.0 / 514.0. Real thread (dense, empty store): `importPreview` round trip 1,718.0 / 1,847.1, `importPrepareApply` round trip 1,440.5 / 1,531.0 (the merged state and findings come back), and the receiving side of the merged state measured as `v8.deserialize`: **130.9 / 150.8 ms** (blocks the caller; D3). **Drift:** the worker-code rows ran before the thread rows and read slower (prepare 2.3 s in the worker code, 1.4 s in the thread round trip that includes it); the machine drifts by about 2x over a run, so rows are not comparable across describes.

**REVIEW REQUIRED**
1. `snapshotBuild` takes `exportedAt` (main's wall-clock time). The plan says `{ revision, reason }`; the worker's clock is monotonic (`performance.now`), and the document carries an export time. Smallest alternative: drop it and stamp the epoch (would make snapshots carry a wrong date).
2. `importRevise` takes `ids` (the plan says `{ batchId, request }`); a revise mints a new batch ID, which needs the per-call data.
3. `importPreview` takes `source: Blob` and `fileName` separately, as the master prompt wrote it (the old stub took an `ImportSource`).
4. A batch that carried asset bytes is used up by `importPrepareApply`'s transfer (the buffers left the worker): after a failed apply of such a batch the user previews again. A batch without assets stays pending after a failed apply, as in Phase 3. Alternative: copy the buffers instead of transferring them.
5. `snapshot-build.ts` repeats the body of `buildSnapshot` (workers do not import persistence). Alternative: a shared package for the codec (a new layer). The duplicated constants are the generator (`organic-reaction-navigator` 0.1.0, the adapter's default) and zlib level 6; the equality test guards the second, not a changed default generator.
6. `storeSnapshotBytes` checks the zlib header only; it does not inflate (up to 200 MB). A wrong `schemaVersion` or a truncated stream is found by `readSnapshot`/restore, as for any stored snapshot.
7. The main thread's receive of the merged state costs about 131 ms mean (151 ms p99) at the design tier (v8.deserialize proxy), on top of the 57-191 ms serialise part of every whole-state send (step 4.2b). Not optimised (D3); judged at Gate E.
8. `prepareApply` builds the merged state's replica (index build + `validateAll`, about 1.4-2.3 s in the worker) although the preview already validated the merged state with the part-1 engine: preview and prepare validate twice in the worker (off the main thread). Alternative: keep the preview's findings and the full index engine from the preview stage (a bigger change to `validateMerged`).

### Step 4.2e — Export in the compute worker (`src/workers/compute`) (2026-09-30)

**Done: a, b, c, d in full; e (no background command or monitor left running).** No new dependency, no schema change. Part A (the 4.2d review record, commit 57a297f) is above.

- **Contract (a).** `buildExport(params): Promise<Blob>` is replaced by `exportPlan({ options, format, revision })` -> `ExportPlanAnswer` (`{ ok: true, assets: { assetId, sha256 }[] }` or `REPLICA_STALE`) and `exportBuild({ options, format, revision, assets: { assetId, sha256, bytes }[], exportedAt })` -> `ExportBuildAnswer` (`ExportBuildResult` or `REPLICA_STALE`). `ExportFormat = 'orn.json' | 'ornpkg'` is new: the plan must know the format, because `.orn.json` reads bytes only for `assets: 'embed'` and `.ornpkg` for `'embed'` and `'package'` (`readsAssetBytes`). Blob is gone from the contract; the result bytes are a `Uint8Array`, transferred (a view onto part of a larger buffer is copied first). Both calls are idempotent (`COMPUTE_SPECS`: plan 30 s, build 60 s).
- **Worker side** (`export-flow.ts`, `handlers.ts`). `planExport` runs the io layer's own `selectScope` over the replica's state and lists the asset records in the closure, in ID order. `buildExportBytes` runs the SAME `buildOrnJsonExport` / `buildOrnPackageExport` as the in-process export, with a provider that is a map lookup over the transferred bytes (an asset main did not send answers `undefined`, so the exporter reports it in `missingAssets`, never thrown). Cancel and progress go through `taskOptionsFrom(ctx)`. `exportedAt` is main's, validated like `snapshotBuild`'s (`assertUtcInstant`, shared). The generator stamp is the snapshot builder's `SNAPSHOT_GENERATOR` (the app's own).
- **Main side (b)** (`export-main.ts`, ports only). `createComputeExport({ sync, store, assetBytes, ids })`: settle the sync, plan for the store's revision, read the listed bytes through the injected `AssetBytesProvider` (persistence's `getAssetBlob` satisfies it once its Blob is read; the real-thread test does exactly that), copy each buffer (so a buffer the provider keeps is never detached) and transfer the copies with the build. A read that throws counts as no bytes and shows up in `missingAssets` (the result has no place for the reason). `REPLICA_STALE` (a commit landed between settle and call) plans again, at most `MAX_EXPORT_ATTEMPTS` = 3 times, then `REJECTED`. `CANCELLED` only when the caller's signal is aborted; a `CANCELLED` from a stopped client is `REJECTED` (a bug the tests found: it read as a user cancel). The export needs only the live state: a failed save does not block it (ADV-040).
- **Tests (c)** (+3 files, +48 tests: 189 / 2,941 -> 192 / 2,989; `npm run check` green as one command). `tests/integration/compute-export.test.ts` (35): INV-19 through the worker, bytes equal to the in-process export for both formats and six scopes (full, chemistry, curriculum, presentation, subset with and without closure) over the minimal fixture, the demo and six generator shapes (tiny), and over the maximal fixture plus five synthetic assets with `assets` none, embed and package (one asset without bytes); what the plan asks main for (only the closure's assets, none when the format reads none); `missingAssets`, a throwing provider, `missingReferences` equal to the in-process ones; structuredClone of every parameter and result; a buffer the provider keeps is not detached; two worker calls per export. `compute-export-failures.test.ts` (11): cancel (already aborted, during main's reads, during the worker's build with the store, revision, history and replica unchanged, the worker-side `CANCELLED` value and progress once per asset plus once for the file), `REPLICA_STALE` (both calls; NOT_READY before the first load; a commit between plan and build gives the newer revision; a replica that keeps moving is `REJECTED` after 3 attempts), ADV-040 (the save fails on quota; the export still builds the unsaved edit, byte-equal to the in-process one), a stopped sync and a crash while building. `compute-export-threads.test.ts` (2): the one real `worker_threads` test of an `.ornpkg` export with assets (bytes read from the real adapter's `getAssetBlob`, unzipped and compared, equal to the in-process export), and an `.orn.json` with embedded assets with a cancel. `tests/property/import-worker-roundtrip.test.ts`: P-02 full is now entirely through the worker, export AND import (27 cases, both exports through `createComputeExport`). New test support: `src/test-support/asset-kit.ts` (synthetic assets: PNG signature, seeded incompressible filler, real SHA-256) and `compute-export-kit.ts`; `compute-rig.ts` logs `exportPlan` and `exportBuild`.

Loaded lazily (a dynamic import on the first call) from the package's own file: in the browser `src/chem/rdkit/wasm-url.ts` imports `@rdkit/rdkit/RDKit_minimal.wasm?url` (a local build asset, no CDN), under Node the glue reads the file next to itself. **dependency-cruiser rule `rdkit-only-in-adapter`**: nothing outside `src/chem/rdkit/` may import `@rdkit/rdkit` (checked by adding a throwaway violation in `src/chem` and in `src/workers`: both reported, then removed; `lint:deps` clean).
- **Eval scan of the glue (a).** Source, `RDKit_minimal.js`: `eval(` **0**; `new Function` **2** (Emscripten embind builds its call wrappers with it: `craftInvokerFunction` and the method caller); `fetch(` 2 and `XMLHttpRequest` (the WASM loading fallbacks, used only with a URL the caller gives); `require("node:fs")` and `require("node:crypto")` only in the Node branch; no `importScripts`, no `import(`, no absolute URL. The same two `new Function` sites are in the lazy chunk of a scratch Vite build. **`new Function` is not allowed by `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`**, so the CSP of SECURITY §4 may stop RDKit at start-up; not testable in Node. See REVIEW REQUIRED 1. Scratch Vite build (not committed): the worker entry bundles to 147 KB, RDKit is its own lazy 64 KB chunk and the WASM a separate hashed 7.3 MB asset the worker references by URL; Vite's **lib mode inlines the WASM as base64 (9.98 MB)**, so the 4.6 build must use the app/worker build, not lib mode.

**What RDKit MinimalLib does here (measured, real RDKit in Node).** A WASM trap (`RuntimeError: memory access out of bounds`, a stack overflow) is reachable well inside the 20,000-character cap: an unbranched chain of 500 atoms works, 700 traps writing the SMILES (parse itself works), 1,000 traps at once; `NCC(=O)` x 400 (2,801 characters) traps; a C++ exception (`WebAssembly.Exception`, no message) came from drawing an 800-heavy-atom amide chain. Some inputs HANG: 4,000 characters of chained cyclohexane rings (`C1CCCCC1` x 500) ran past 25 s, and the depiction of 10,001 disconnected `C` atoms (20,000 characters) also runs past the limit. So the size caps are not a bound on RDKit's work: the 2 s limit with terminate-and-restart is the defence, and traps must be caught. `get_mol` returns `null` for a structure it cannot read (it throws only in rare cases). Logging goes to stderr/console unless switched off (`disable_logging()` is called at load).

- **Adapter (b)** (`src/chem/rdkit/`: `adapter.ts` 186 lines, `facts.ts`, `draw.ts`, `scope.ts`, `smiles-atoms.ts`, `elements.ts`, `errors.ts`, `types.ts`, `loader.ts`, `wasm-url.ts`; plus `src/chem/depiction-options.ts`, `lru.ts`, `cached-toolkit.ts`). `createRdkitToolkit({ load })` implements `StructureToolkit`; the module is loaded on the first call, concurrent first calls share one load, `ready()` never rejects and a failed load is not remembered. **Caps and format BEFORE RDKit**: SMILES and CXSMILES 20,000 characters, molfile 1,000,000 (`LIMITS`), empty or unknown format, and the declared format is checked because `get_mol` sniffs its input (a "SMILES" with a line break or a brace, a "molfile" without `M  END`, are `invalid`). **`ParseOutcome` reasons (Q7)**: `invalid` (RDKit cannot read the structure, an over-cap input; the only reason that means the structure is bad), `unavailable` (no module, a WASM trap, or a failure while WORKING on a structure RDKit did read, such as drawing it), `timeout` (only the RPC client says it, below). A trap or a JS `RangeError` drops the module (the next call loads a fresh one, measured 44 ms in a real thread). **One helper frees every RDKit object** (`withHandle`, a `finally`): `scope.test.ts` proves with a fake module that it frees on success, on a throw, on an early return inside the callback, with nested handles (inner first), never frees twice, hides no failing `delete()` on a normal path and does not let a failing `delete()` replace an exception already propagating (after a trap `delete()` can trap too); the adapter tests assert `fake.leaked()` is empty after every operation and every failure path.
- **Facts, and what is left undefined (b).** `canonicalSmiles` is RDKit's canonical isomeric SMILES **with atom map numbers kept** (MinimalLib cannot strip them: `ignoreAtomMapNumbers` has no effect, so a mapped structure and its unmapped twin have different canonical SMILES; matters for CHEM-009 in 4.3b). `formula` is a Hill formula the ADAPTER computes from RDKit's own JSON (atomic numbers and implicit hydrogens; all components summed, no charge, no isotopes) because MinimalLib has no formula call; undefined if an atom is a dummy or not in the table. `charge` is the sum of formal charges from that JSON. `heavyAtomCount` is `get_num_atoms(true)`. `specifiedStereocentres`, `unspecifiedStereocentres`, `hasDoubleBondStereo` come from `get_stereo_tags()` (`(?)` = not specified; a specified double bond means E or Z). `aromatic` is "any aromatic atom" from the JSON's representation extension. `atomMaps` are read from RDKit's own canonical SMILES (MinimalLib has no accessor), ascending with repeats kept. **Left undefined, never guessed, with a warning that names the fact:** any fact RDKit does not give for that structure (a stereo-tag exception leaves the three stereo facts undefined; a missing representation extension leaves `aromatic` undefined; a dummy atom leaves `formula` undefined; unreadable JSON leaves formula, charge and aromatic undefined). **`warnings` is only the adapter's own per-fact notes (at most 10)**: MinimalLib gave no parse warnings (`set_log_capture` returned an empty buffer while RDKit still wrote its message to stderr), so RDKit's own warnings are not reported. For the demo, 64 of the 65 species with a structure parse and give EVERY fact with no warning (asserted); the 65th is the invalid SMILES, and one species has no structure.
- **Depiction (b).** `depict` always returns sanitised SVG or a failure value; the key is `hash(format, value, options, toolkit, version)`. RDKit draws atom map numbers as part of the atom label and has no option to hide them, so with `showAtomMaps: false` the structure is drawn again from RDKit's canonical SMILES without the `:n` (a molfile's coordinates are then lost; only when the structure has maps). A highlight by `highlightAtomMaps` finds its atoms through the SMILES and RDKit's `_smilesAtomOutputOrder`; if they cannot be located the depiction is `unavailable`, not drawn wrongly. Bad options are a programmer error (`RangeError`; the worker host answers `BAD_REQUEST`).
- **Chem worker (c)** (`src/workers/chem/`: `handlers.ts`, `host.ts`, `entry.ts`, `specs.ts`, `client.ts`). Handlers over the adapter behind the cache; the shape of every param is checked at the wire (`BAD_REQUEST`), the content is the toolkit's. Specs: `parse` and `depict` idempotent, **2,000 ms** each. `createChemService(client)` (main side) turns a call the worker could not answer into a value: `TIMEOUT` -> `timeout` (not retried, D4), everything else -> `unavailable` with the code; a crash under a call is retried once. Restart is the RPC client's: a call past its limit terminates the thread and starts a new one, which loads the WASM again on its first call. **Cache**: two LRU caches of 500 entries (facts, depictions) in the worker, key hash(kind, format, value, options, toolkit, version); a hit also compares the whole input, so a hash collision cannot answer for another structure (tested with a hash forced to collide); `invalid` and `refused` are cached, `unavailable` and `timeout` never. The worker entry is `entry.ts`; creating it in the app is Phase 5 (D7).
- **Sanitiser (d)** (`src/chem/svg/`: `sanitize.ts` 185 lines, `tag.ts`, `attributes.ts`, `values.ts`, `whitelist.ts`, `text.ts`), rules in SECURITY §2. One linear pass, the open-element stack capped at 256 (deeper is refused, no recursion), no DOMParser. The output is written from whitelisted parts with escaping; it always starts with its own `xmlns`, is idempotent and no string in it contains `href`, `url(`, `expression`, `javascript` or an `on...=` in any case (a second, independent check on every attribute value and text node, on top of the value patterns). Refusals are values with a reason: `too_large` (over **2 MiB**, the message says so), `declaration` (DOCTYPE or any other `<!`), `too_deep`, `no_svg`. Everything else it drops is counted in the report. RDKit's own output needs `stroke-miterlimit` (found by the real-RDKit test on 1-bromopropane, added to the whitelist).

**Tests (e)** (+11 files, +282 tests: 194 / 3,000 -> 205 / 3,282 after Part A; `npm run check` green as ONE command).

- `src/chem/rdkit/adapter.test.ts` (28, fake module: lazy loading, caps before RDKit, formats, every reason, traps, the stage that decides the reason, depiction through the sanitiser, keys, atom maps, SMARTS), `scope.test.ts` (9), `facts.test.ts` (21), `src/chem/cache.test.ts` (24: LRU, cache rules, option checks), `cache-collision.test.ts` (2), `src/workers/chem/handlers.test.ts` (19: in-memory port with `structuredClone` of every message, `BAD_REQUEST`, cache use, the service's `timeout` and `unavailable`, one retry after a crash), `tests/types/rpc-contracts.test.ts` (+1).

Canonical SMILES is a fixed point for every species. **REVIEW REQUIRED**
1. **CSP and `new Function`.** RDKit's glue calls `new Function` (embind) in two places; `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` does not allow it. Also, `vite.config.ts` injects the CSP as a `<meta>` tag, and a meta policy is not applied to a dedicated worker (its policy comes from its own script's response headers). Both must be checked in the 4.6 build smoke; if RDKit needs `'unsafe-eval'`, that is a security decision (SECURITY §4 says the CSP is `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` only), not one to make silently. Recorded in SECURITY §4 as open.
2. **Contract changes (Amendments below).** `ParseOutcome` failures carry `reason` (Q7, approved); `depict` answers `DepictOutcome` (a value with `refused` as a fourth reason) instead of a bare `Depiction`, and `matchesSmarts` answers `SmartsOutcome` instead of `boolean | 'invalid_smarts'`, because neither could say "invalid structure", "toolkit unavailable" or "drawing refused" (CLAUDE.md §6: errors across a module boundary are values); and `ChemWorkerApi.checkAll` is removed now (Q2 approved its replacement in 4.3b; a host could not implement a method that assumes state in a stateless worker). `StructureToolkit.ready()` resolves when loading has finished, successfully or not.
3. **An input that traps RDKit is `unavailable`, not `invalid`** (the toolkit crashed; the structure may be fine), so CHEM-001 does not fire for it and it is checked again, and crashes again, on every check (about 30-45 ms each, nothing is cached). If a deterministic crash should count as a bad structure, that is a decision for 4.3b.
4. **Declared format is enforced** (a SMILES with a line break or a brace, a molfile without `M  END`, are `invalid`) because RDKit sniffs its input. Not in the master prompt; small and cheap; say if it should go.
5. **`formula` is computed by the adapter** (Hill, from RDKit's JSON), `atomMaps` from RDKit's canonical SMILES, `canonicalSmiles` keeps map numbers, `warnings` holds only the adapter's per-fact notes (see above). The stored `species.formula` strings of the demo (`C2H5OH`, `CH3COOH`) are not Hill and are not compared with it here; CHEM-002/003 (4.3b) decide what to do with that.
6. **Hiding atom maps redraws from the SMILES** (a molfile's coordinates are lost, only when it has maps).
7. Real-browser start-up of the chem worker (WASM fetch from the build asset, cold init in a bundled worker) is not measured here.

**Open items.** See PROJECT_STATE openItems (the CSP question, Phase 5 wiring of the chem worker and `createChemService`, no baseline for the new bench).

- **a. CHEM-006** (`src/chem/checks/stereo.ts`, pure; `species.ts` calls it). Compares ONLY the multiset of R/S letters and of E/Z letters in the species' descriptors with RDKit's CIP labels (new additive fact `StructureFacts.cipCounts`, from the same `get_stereo_tags` call). A descriptor is read only in the form `[locant]R|S|E|Z` (comma, semicolon or slash lists, optional parentheses); anything else is words. "Not compared" (in `statusOf(...).notCompared`, never a finding): words-only or other forms, lower-case r/s in a descriptor or in the structure, unspecified stereocentres in the structure, R/S naming FEWER centres that fit inside the structure's, and E/Z counts that differ (RDKit does not list a double bond whose geometry is not given, so an unequal count may be an unspecified bond: only an equal count with different letters is a finding). A finding (WARNING, path `stereo.descriptors`) only for a certain disagreement: a different letter at equal count, more R/S centres named than the structure has, a letter it lacks. - **Request checks.** `checkRequest` (`src/layout/validate.ts`, shared by the worker and the service): `TOO_LARGE` over the caps; `BAD_REQUEST` for unsorted or duplicate ids, an edge to a missing node, non-finite sizes (at least 1), spacing, seed (unsigned 32-bit integer), hints (integer 0 to 10,000) or positions, unknown algorithm or direction. In the worker both are `BAD_REQUEST` (the too-large message starts `TOO_LARGE:`); the service refuses both as values before any call.
- **ELK adapter (b)** (`src/layout/elk/`). `LayoutEngine` over a fresh ELK instance per layout (no state shared between calls). Layered: direction, node/layer/edge spacing, seed (`elk.randomSeed`), zero padding. Radial and stress: ring radius and desired edge length are `spacing.layer` plus the largest node dimension (ELK measures them between centres). **Seed** is passed to ELK as `elk.randomSeed`; on stress it changes the layout (tested), on layered and radial it is passed and no effect was seen.
  **Hints, measured on elkjs 0.12.0** (the table is at the top of `map-request.ts`, proved by `tests/integration/layout-elk.test.ts`):
  - layered `layerHint`: honoured as the ORDER of layers (ELK partitions; a lower hint is never to the right of a higher one), not as exact layer numbers; no note. `layerChoiceConstraint` did nothing in 0.12.0 and is not used.
  - layered `orderHint`: honoured as a PREFERENCE (children listed in hint order, `considerModelOrder` = `PREFER_NODES`; `NODES_AND_EDGES` let edge order override the hints); no note. Not used when `previous` is (noted).
  - layered `previous`: honoured as the order inside layers (interactive crossing minimisation with the previous positions); a node without one takes the mean of its positioned neighbours, else the far end; a `previous` that names no node of the request is noted.
  - `pinned`: NOT honoured by any ELK algorithm (layered has no fixed positions; stress's `fixed` option did not hold in 0.12.0), ignored AND noted with a count.
  - layered edge `priority`: honoured (`layered.priority.direction`); ignored and noted by radial and stress.
  - radial: `layerHint` only chooses the root of each tree (noted); `orderHint`, `previous` ignored (noted). stress: `layerHint`, `orderHint`, `previous` ignored (noted).
  - `direction` applies to layered only (radial and stress have none; not a hint, not noted).

  **Two ELK facts found and handled.** (1) ELK radial throws "The given graph is not a tree!" for any graph with a cycle, a parallel edge or a loop, and overlaps nodes on a forest: the adapter builds a spanning tree (BFS per component, root = lowest `layerHint`, else most connected, ties by id), joins several components under ONE virtual size-0 centre node (dropped from the answer), gives ELK only tree edges and draws the rest straight, all counted in `notes`. (2) Radial and stress ignore node sizes, so wide nodes overlapped (measured on the first run): `spread.ts` scales the centres apart by the smallest factor that separates every pair by the node gap (every edge then drawn straight, noted); coincident centres or a factor over 20 are an ELK failure (the worker answers with the fallback, `elk_error`; seen once on the hub_explosion precursor explorer with radial).
- **Fallback (c)** (`src/layout/fallback/`, pure). Cycle breaking: iterative DFS, roots and edges in id order, back edges reversed. Longest-path layering over the DAG in Kahn order; `layerHint` places a node EXACTLY on its layer (an edge between two hinted nodes may point backwards); empty layers are squeezed out. **Barycentric ordering: 8 sweeps** (`SWEEPS`, four downward, four upward, alternating), stable; after every sort the nodes carrying an `orderHint` are put back into the slots hinted nodes occupy in (hint, id) order, so among hinted nodes of a layer the hint decides. Complexity: barycentres O(V + E) per sweep, plus an O(m log m) sort per layer (so a sweep is O(V + E + V log V); not strictly O(V + E)). Positions from node sizes and spacing (layers a layer gap apart, nodes a node gap apart, layers centred on the widest; LEFT and UP mirror RIGHT and DOWN); straight border-to-border routes, a four-point loop for a self-loop; parallel edges draw on top of each other. No two node boxes overlap, by construction, and tested (every direction, odd sizes, 400 / 800, the caps). It ignores `pinned`, `previous` and edge `priority` and the algorithm (it is always layered); each is noted. `seed` is accepted and unused.
- **Worker and service (d).** `src/workers/layout`: `entry.ts` imports `zod-jitless` first (ADR-035) and starts `startLayoutHost`; `layout` answers ELK's result or the fallback with `elk_error` (ELK threw; a note names what it said) or `engine_unavailable` (ELK could not load); `layoutFallback` answers the fallback alone for the reason given. Specs: both idempotent, 2,000 ms. `createLayoutService` (ports only: an `RpcClient<LayoutWorkerApi>`): per-call limit 2 s (override per call); on TIMEOUT the RPC client has terminated and restarted the worker and the service asks the NEW worker for the fallback (`'timeout'`); other failures (crash twice, busy, not ready) get the fallback with `'engine_unavailable'`; if that fails too the result is `{ ok: false, code: 'UNAVAILABLE' }`, never a main-thread layout. A newer request for the same view cancels the older (`CANCELLED`, result dropped; a running ELK still finishes in the worker). **Cache: LRU of 32** results by `cacheKey`, memory only (persistence is Phase 5); cached: ELK answers and the `elk_error` fallback; NOT cached: `timeout` and `engine_unavailable` fallbacks. **Caps: 2,000 nodes, 4,000 edges** refused as values (`TOO_LARGE`).
- **Test-support.** `src/test-support/layout-kit.ts` (sorted requests, a seeded random graph, validity checks, the projection mapper with fixed 120 x 40 node sizes), `layout-projections.ts` (demo and design tier navigator, reaction explorer, precursor explorer), `layout-fakes.ts` (a fake ELK), `spawnLayoutWorker` in `rpc-node-port.ts`, fixture `tests/fixtures/layout/worker.ts` (modes `real`, `busy` = an uninterruptible synchronous loop, `throw`).

**Tests (e).** Files 221, tests 3,572. New: `src/layout/layout.test.ts` (checks, key, LRU, routes), `src/layout/fallback/fallback.test.ts` (19), `src/layout/elk/elk.test.ts` (fake ELK: mapping, radial tree, spread, failure modes), `src/workers/layout/layout.test.ts` (18: in-memory port with every message cloned, the specs, handlers, refusals, cache and LRU, supersede, the timeout path with a fake engine, no worker able to answer, a crash retried once, two crashes), `tests/integration/layout-elk.test.ts` (40, REAL elkjs: valid layouts for three algorithms on chains, cycles, loops, parallel edges, disconnected graphs, empty and single; every hint row of the table; the seed; **determinism property: the same request gives byte-identical positions and routes from fresh instances and from a reused one, ELK 60 runs and the fallback 150 runs, durationMs excluded**; the key moves with every real change), `tests/integration/layout-projections.test.ts` (35: the real demo and design-tier projections, three algorithms, valid and structured-clone safe, deterministic, the fallback valid and fast), `tests/integration/layout-worker-threads.test.ts` (5, a REAL thread: a layout with real ELK for all three algorithms; **the timeout path with a thread that cannot be interrupted: TIMEOUT at 500 ms, the thread terminated, a NEW thread answers the fallback `timeout`, the 8 s loop is not waited for**; `elk_error`; refusals never reach the thread; the worker's own BAD_REQUEST). ### Step 4.5 — Search worker (`src/search`, `src/workers/search`) (2026-10-01)

**Done: a, b, c, d, e, f, g (h not needed: nothing left over).** `npm run check` green as ONE command: 228 files, 3,675 tests, Vitest 101.0 s, whole command 2 min 6 s (was 221 / 3,580 after Part A). Commit A (the 4.4 review follow-ups) is the commit before this one. No schema change, no `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump. No background command or monitor left running.

- **Contracts (CLAUDE.md §7; Amendments).** Q6 as approved: `SearchDocument.scopeRanks` (exam version id to rank 0 official ... 3 outside; a record the version does not map has no rank), `lifecycle`, `SearchQuery.examVersionId`, `SearchIndexUpdate.fromRevision`, `apply` answers `ApplyAnswer`, `serialize()` / `loadSerialized({ json, revision })`. Beyond Q6 (REVIEW REQUIRED 1): `SearchDocument.aliases` (so a hit can say it matched an alias; `names` no longer holds aliases), `textTruncated`, `facets.scopes` defined (distinct scope names, best first), `SearchHit.score` rounded to 9 decimals, the limits `SEARCH_TEXT_CAP` 4,000, `MAX_QUERY_CHARS` 1,000, `MAX_QUERY_WORDS` 16, `MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT` 200, and the old `SearchService` interface became `SearchEngine` (the index itself); `SearchWorkerApi` gains `serialize` and `loadSerialized`, `apply` answers a value, `search` is `NOT_READY` before a load.
- **What each document contains (b).** The header of `src/search/document/builder.ts` and SEARCH §6 have the full list. Every kind: title, names, aliases, entered formula (species, class, reagent), structure text (species, class), tags, plain text of its OWN rich text and fields, lifecycle, review status. Species: names, aliases, formula, structure, isotope note, stereo descriptors and note, properties, acid-base, study and general notes. Class: formula text and general formula (as the formula), generic structure, R-group note, description, notes. Reagent: names, aliases plus every profile's label and aliases, formula text, profile behaviours, description, notes. Reaction: name, aliases, generalised equation, the original wording, labels and notes of participants, stages, variants, outcomes, products and intermediates, reversibility, selectivity, limitations, notes. Named reaction, concept, transformation, mechanism (variants and steps), caveat (title, rule, statement, trigger, explanation), route (description, step notes), topic, reference (title, authors, edition, publisher, identifier, year, notes). Not indexed: relationships, exams, exam versions, topic mappings, exam relevance, assets, presentation records (tested on the demo, which has presentation records).
  **Does a document contain text of OTHER records? No.** A reaction does not carry its participants' names (ids stay ids), a species does not carry its classes' names. So a rename, an alias or a note on a record refreshes that one document, and renaming the 1,000-referrer hub is one document (tested: a reaction's document is byte-identical after its participant is renamed). What a document does read from elsewhere is DERIVED, not text: `scopeRanks` / `facets.scopes` (core's `scopeOf` per exam version), `facets.topicIds` (mapped topics and their ancestors), and for a reaction `facets.reagentFamilies` (the families of its reagent participants). Those are what item d refreshes. Consequence (REVIEW REQUIRED 2): searching "ethanol" finds the species, not the reactions that use it; that is the navigator's job (SEARCH §3 lists no such field).
- **MiniSearch configuration (c)** (`src/search/engine/config.ts`, `query.ts`). Fields name, alias (boost 4, prefix ON, fuzzy by length), formula (3, exact), structure (2, exact, the trimmed text as ONE case-sensitive term), tags (2) and text (1) (no prefix, fuzzy by length). Terms come from core's `tokens()` (folded words, adjacent pairs, whole phrase joined), body text word by word so it does not triple the index. Fuzzy: 1 edit at 5+ characters, 2 at 9+, none shorter (characters, not UTF-16 units). Prefix, fuzzy and exactness are set per query GROUP (names and aliases; formulas; tags and text) through query-combination options, because MiniSearch applies them per query, not per field. Ranking: score (rounded to 9 decimals), exam-version scope rank (only when the query names a version), published before draft, folded title, id: a total order. Kinds and facets filter (any value within a facet, all facets; an empty list is no constraint; with an exam version the scope facet is read under it). No words with a filter lists what the filter admits (a palette prefix alone); no words and no filter lists nothing.
  **Facts found and handled.** (1) MiniSearch's `discard` leaves old postings until a vacuum, so document counts, and with them scores, would depend on the history of updates and searches: removal uses `remove` with the stored document, so the index is a function of its documents. (2) BM25's average field length drifts by a few ulps with the add/remove history: scores are rounded to 9 decimals, which lets an incrementally maintained index and a fresh one agree on hits AND order. (3) A first draft let the joined form of a multi-word query be fuzzy; "Reaction 41" then also matched every "reaction" (two edits): the joined form is now names and aliases only, prefix, no fuzzy.
- **Incremental updates (d)** (`src/workers/search`). `apply` with `fromRevision`; the worker answers `{ ok, revision, upserted, removed }` or `REVISION_MISMATCH` with `have` (-1: nothing loaded); everything is validated before any change (a malformed update changes nothing). The main-side sync (`sync.ts`, ports only: state, the full indexes, the store revision, the search service, a debounce `schedule`) rebuilds the change's own records and, via `fanout.ts`, every document whose derived data another record's change moved: a topic mapping or exam relevance (the target before AND after, the old one read from the inverse patches), a reagent whose families changed (its reactions), a prerequisite field, a relationship or any mapping (every concept: a concept's derived scope depends on the direct scope of what it is a prerequisite of), an exam version whose units or exam changed, a topic deleted or re-parented (everything). Field changes are found by comparing the old record (from the inverse patch) with the new one, because the store's patches replace whole records. Dependent documents are queued 500 at a time (`REFRESH_CAP`), the rest in a backlog behind them, never dropped; only documents that differ from the one last sent (a hash is remembered per record) are sent; an update that changes no document still advances the index revision (the warm-boot cache is keyed by it). `replace` and `remote` changes, a mismatch and any worker failure lead to ONE full load of the current state (the previous index keeps answering until it lands); a failing worker leaves the sync `down` with the reason and the next trigger loads again. `serialize` / `loadSerialized` carry one JSON text (MiniSearch's export, the documents, the format version, the configuration id); a text that does not load is `BAD_INDEX` as a value and leaves the engine as it was. The service supersedes per channel (a newer query cancels the older: `CANCELLED`).
  **Hand mutants:** 11 mutations of the fan-out rules (old target, new target, concept fan-out for a mapping, for a relationship, for a prerequisite field, reagent families, exam version units, topic parent, field-change detection forced false and forced true, direct records skipped), all KILLED. Two mutants first SURVIVED and taught something: "exam record created" (the rule was dead: `scopeOf` never reads an exam record, only its id, so the rule was removed) and "topic created" (a new topic reaches nothing, whatever points at it is a change of its own: narrowed to deletion).
- **Palette grammar (e)** (`src/search/palette/parse.ts`, pure): plain text; `r: s: c: g: n: m: t:` narrow to reaction, species, class, reagent, named reaction, mechanism, topic; `>` commands (text lower-cased, spaces collapsed). Case and whitespace tolerant, a full-width colon counts; only the first prefix is read; reads at most 1,064 characters; cuts to 16 words and 1,000 characters and reports `truncated`.

**Tests (f).** `src/search/engine/engine.test.ts` (29: C2H5OH = C₂H₅OH, Wolff-Kishner = wolffkishner, α = alpha, the query parts agree with core `tokens()` for random input, prefix on names only, fuzzy by term length at 4, 5, 8, 9 characters, formulas and structures exact, the order and its tie-breaks, any load order and updates give the same answers, what a hit matched, filters and facets, revisions and refusals, serialise round trips and nine kinds of bad index, structuredClone of every param and result), `src/search/palette/parse.test.ts` (18, fast-check: never throws, within limits, linear), `src/search/document/builder.test.ts` (14: kinds, contents, no text of other records, the cap including a surrogate pair, scope ranks against `scopeOf`, topics, reagent families), `src/workers/search/search.test.ts` (19: the worker over RPC with every message cloned, refusals as values, NOT_READY, supersede, ordinary and curriculum updates, **ADV-019 search half**, **ADV-058 search part**, the 500 cap with a backlog of 1,040 reactions, mismatch and one full load, a crashed worker, a failing worker), `src/workers/search/fanout.test.ts` (10), **`tests/property/search-incremental.test.ts` (3, THE property: after random command sequences of renames, aliases, tags, lifecycle, notes, creations, deletions, mappings, relevance, coverage, topic edits, prerequisites, families, undo, redo and a replaceState, the incrementally maintained index holds exactly the documents of a full build and answers a generated query set of about 200 queries (titles, prefixes, typos, aliases, formulas, structures, facets, exam versions) with the same hits, order and scores as an index rebuilt from scratch; flushing after every step or only at the end gives the same index; the walk is not vacuous: every edit kind, undo, redo and replace are reached)**, `tests/integration/search-worker-threads.test.ts` (2, a REAL thread: boot from a store, edits flow, answers equal an in-process index, supersede, a second thread booted alike, the serialised index loads in another thread, NOT_READY before a load, an `apply` mismatch).

**Benchmarks (g)** (`tests/perf/search.bench.ts`, 15 entries in `tests/perf/budgets-search.mjs`, run once alone with `npm run bench`; no `bench:baseline`, no `bench:compare`), mean / p99 ms, worker code in Node, the design tier dense shape (5,000 reactions, 2,000 other entities, 10 topics, two exam versions, formulas on the species); this machine moves by 20 to 40 percent between runs:
- Queries (row: < 50 ms p95, judged on p99): name prefix "Reaction 41" 27.8 / 42.5; fuzzy name "Reactin 4100" 4.8 / 7.7; exact formula 0.16 / 0.95; palette-prefixed "r: Reaction 4100" 25.9 / 48.2. Informal worst cases: a prefix every reaction matches ("reacti") 33.2 / 58.0 (73.7 in another run); fuzzy over every species ("specias") 2.6 / 5.8.
  Why the prefix rows are slow: the synthetic names are "Reaction N", so the joined-pair terms of core's `tokens()` ("reaction41", "reaction42", ...) give 5,000 distinct terms that start with "reaction", and a prefix on "reaction" scores all of them. Real names are far more varied; this is the adversarial case. The two prefix rows pass on p99 with a thin margin (a first version, before the joined form lost its fuzzy match, read 58 ms p99 on "Reaction 41").
- Full builds (SEARCH §5 row: < 1.5 s): the index from the documents (worker) 177.0 / 218.6, so the row is met with a large margin. Every document built from the state on the MAIN thread: 869.8 / 934.9 with the indexes built too, 192.6 / 210.8 with the indexes ready (the builder and `scopeOf` alone). serialize 131.6 / 157.3; loadSerialized 126.9 / 164.1 (about the same as a build here, the synthetic documents are small).
- Incremental: the worker takes one document (apply) 0.18 / 0.59; the sync end to end, an ordinary edit (change analysis, document build, hash, in-process engine) 0.13 / 0.43; the rename of the 1,000-referrer hub 0.15 / 0.68 (documents hold no other record's name, so it is one document, the same cost); a curriculum edit that moves every document (an exam version's coverage), 6,998 documents rebuilt and hashed 500 at a time, only the changed sent: 302.8 / 379.3 in all, about 22 ms per slice of 500.

**REVIEW REQUIRED**
1. **Contract additions beyond Q6** (above): `aliases`, `textTruncated`, `facets.scopes` shape, the limits, `SearchService` renamed `SearchEngine`, `serialize` / `loadSerialized` on the worker API. Approve, or say what else.
2. **A document never holds another record's text**, so a reaction is not found by its participants' names (searching "ethanol" finds the species). It keeps renames to one document and makes the 1,000-referrer hub rename cost nothing. If a view needs "reactions of ethanol" by search, say so: it would be a field of the reaction document and a fan-out from every rename of a participant.
3. **Derived formulas** (SEARCH §3 says "entered or derived"): documents carry the ENTERED formula only; a formula derived from a structure needs the chem worker and its facts; wiring that is Phase 5.
4. **Prefix applies to every query word**, as SEARCH §3 says ("prefix search on names"), not only the last. It is what makes broad prefixes cost about 30 ms on the adversarial synthetic names. Prefix on the last word only would cut that to about 10 ms and is the usual type-ahead rule; it changes behaviour ("eth acid" would no longer find "ethanoic acid"). Decide.
5. **Fuzzy and transpositions:** edit distance 1 at 5 to 8 characters, as specified, counts a swap of two letters as two edits, so "Reactoin" does not find "Reaction". A Damerau distance is not in MiniSearch.
6. **Main-thread cost of a full load:** building every document on the main thread is 193 ms with the indexes ready (870 ms with the indexes built too) at the design tier, above a frame, for a boot, a `replace`, a `remote` change or a mismatch; a curriculum edit that moves everything is about 22 ms per slice of 500 (over 16 ms). Options for Phase 5/9: a smaller `REFRESH_CAP` (250), or build the documents in the compute worker, which already holds the replica and the indexes (the builder is pure and takes ports; the sync would then ask the worker for the update). Not done: the 4.5 text asks for a main-side sync.
7. **The sync needs the FULL indexes** (`ReadonlyIndexes`: topics, relationships), which the store does not expose (it keeps `CoreIndexes`); the test rig keeps them as the app will, applying each ChangeSet with `indexEngine.apply`. Phase 5 must provide the same port.
8. **Scores are rounded to 9 decimals** in `SearchHit.score` (needed for incremental = rebuild, see above).

| Q | answer (fits / gap) | gap and smallest amendment (landing step) |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 Indexes on main | gap | The store maintains only `coreIndexEngine` (`getIndexes()` returns `CoreIndexes`: no `navigatorRollup`, participations, `topicsOf`, `displayOf`). The navigator needs `navigatorRollup()` through `ProjectionContext.indexes`; the search sync needs the full `ReadonlyIndexes` (its port); the L4 service needs only `referrersOf` / `descendantsOf` and is already served by `getIndexes()` (fits). The full engine does NOT support the one-step-back rollback: `apply` calls `build` whenever `changes.revision !== core.revision + 1` (src/core/indexes/full.ts), so a rejected commit on a full-engine store would rebuild (about 0.5 s); its handles are one mutable lineage (an older handle throws "Stale index handle"); and the derived tables take about 300 ms of the 448 ms hub edit (open item 58) against the 16 / 50 ms commit rows. Option A (store takes the full engine) therefore breaks the commit rows on hub edits. Smallest amendment (option B, no core change): an app-level `DerivedIndexes` service in `src/app/services`: builds `indexEngine.build(state, revision)` lazily on the first read; `store.subscribe` queues ChangeSets; a read applies them in order (a `replace` / `remote` cause, a gap, or a queue over a bound -> one `build`); `current()` returns the handle for the store's revision and callers never keep it past the call. Rejected commits are never announced, so no rollback exists on this path. Cost: the hub edit's 300-450 ms lands on main at the first read after it, off the commit path; 5.1a benches it and the reviewer judges. Landing: 5.1a. |
| Q2 Store and findings for React | fits | `getState()` and `getRevision()` keep their identity until a commit (frozen Immer state); `subscribe(listener)` fires after each commit, with the ChangeSet as an argument that a `useSyncExternalStore` subscriber ignores; `canUndo()` / `canRedo()` are booleans (valid snapshots). `FindingStore.counts()` returns one frozen object per change (no scan on read; the recount is a scan of all findings per change, not measured), and includes `review_required`; `bySubject` is cached; `all()` without a filter is cached (with a filter it returns a new array: not a snapshot). Notes: `historyLabels()` builds new arrays on every call (read on demand for a tooltip, never as a snapshot); L4 results change the finding store WITHOUT a ChangeSet, so React needs a second subscription (finding store). No amendment; selector hooks are built in 5.1c (`src/ui/hooks`). |
| Q3 Projections | gap | `ProjectionRequest` (view, focus, expansion, filters, limits with signal) fits the UI. But `navigatorProjection.build` never reads `request.expansion` or `request.focus` (src/core/graph/navigator/build.ts: its header says "Not built yet: hub expansion/focus, degree caps and overflow"; it shows every real hub plus Unclassified and one arrow per outcome product, truncated at `maxEdges`): hub expansion DOES NOT EXIST in the navigator projection, although GRAPH_SEMANTICS §3 and §11 define it and plan step 5.5a needs it. A memo "by request and the revisions of the records read" does not exist either: `Projection.key` is documented as "request + revision of every dependency record" but `projectionKey(request, revision)` hashes the store's global revision, so it changes on every commit, and no read-set is recorded anywhere. The 5.5a counter test then uses an edit of a kind the view does not read (for example a reference or a presentation record). Landing: (1) a new core step ahead of 5.5a, to be placed at the contract decisions; (2) 5.5a. |

**Plan observations (reviewer to decide; the plan text above is unchanged).**

1. Seeding comes after its first use. ADV-012's e2e part (5.5a) needs a 1,000-reaction dataset in the browser, but the import UI is 5.9a and the first run offers only the demo. Either the e2e seeds IndexedDB from test code (Q12, recommended, no production code) or a minimal "Import file" moves ahead of 5.5a. I would take the seed helper.
2. The navigator has no hub expansion in core (Q3). The plan lists "hub expand and collapse" inside 5.5a as UI work, but the projection ignores `expansion`, degree caps and overflow. It needs its own core step with a bench before 5.5a, or 5.5a becomes two steps and the user's first look at the app slips.
3. Step 5.1b is two steps. Chem + L4 + layout + search sync + warm cache + the start-up limit is one session; the three whole-state flows (import, restore, export) with their ports and the one-operation rule are another. Split at the line between the engines and the flows. 5.1a is also near the limit once periodic snapshots, markers and the lint rules (Q6, Q10) are added; consider moving the lint rules to a tiny step 5.0.
4. Missing from the plan: periodic snapshots, the clean-shutdown and integrity markers, persistent-storage request and storage estimate (Q6), and notices for `crashSuspected`, quarantined rows and asset problems from the boot report (nothing silent, CLAUDE.md §1.5).
5. E7 says "no second code path" for Load demo, but a down compute worker leaves import with no path (`createComputeImport` answers `REJECTED`). Restore and export offer an in-process fallback; import should too, as a value, or the first run can strand a user whose worker cannot start. The cost is one more flow test in 5.1b.
6. The CSP result changes 5.2 (Q11): Radix Dialog, Popover, Menu, Select and ScrollArea inject `<style>` in their default form. Put an E3 spike at the start of 5.2 (render each planned primitive in the production build with the CSP and assert zero violations) before building the design system on them; the page is cheap to throw away, the primitives are not.
7. Cross-engine risk is left to the end. Firefox and WebKit appear first in 5.10a: module workers, WASM, Web Locks, BroadcastChannel and IndexedDB blobs differ there. Run a two-spec smoke (boots, demo loads, worker parses) in all three engines from 5.1c, and keep the full suite in 5.10a.
8. The e2e CSP proof is weaker than ADR-035 reads (Q13 b): a `<meta>` CSP does not reach workers. Add the header project, or change SECURITY §4 to say the worker half is a build-smoke check only.
9. Persisting depictions in `derivedCache` (PERFORMANCE §8: 100 MB soft cap) is in no step; 5.4a says LRU in memory only. Either say Phase 9 owns the persistent cache (my preference: the memory LRU is enough for Gate E) or add it to 5.4a with a quota test.
10. Undo and redo in the top bar (5.8, E9) can never be enabled in Phase 5: the only commits are import and Undo import, and `replaceState` clears the history (ADV-045). Show them disabled with the reason ("nothing to undo; editing arrives in Phase 6", E8) and take the store-binding test to Phase 6, or keep a small test with a synthetic commit.
11. The search remedy named in 5.1b ("a remedy proposal" for the 193 ms document build) cannot be "build documents in the compute worker" without an amendment: the `worker-entry-compute` rule forbids `src/search`. Say that in the proposal; moving the pure builder under core, or lifting that rule for the builder only, are the two options.
12. 5.5a asks the user to try the app with only the demo and no import, no search and no inspector. That is fine for a navigator check, but the inspector (5.6a) is what makes clicks useful. Consider reordering 5.6a before the user's look, or keep the checkpoint and tell the user what is not there yet.
13. The 80% coverage line for `src/render/scene` and `src/app/services` joins in 5.3, but `src/app/services` is created in 5.1a. Add it in 5.1a; add `src/features` and `src/ui` as informal figures only (component code, jsdom).
14. A bundle has no step. GRAPH_SEMANTICS §11 draws parallel edges as one path with a count badge and says expanding the bundle fans them out; the overflow node "opens a virtualised list". 5.3 builds `bundleSize` and the overflow glyph, but nothing in 5.5 to 5.7 selects a bundle, lists its reactions (inspector) or fans it out. Add both to 5.5b (selection and inspector list) and say whether the fan-out itself waits for Phase 7.
15. "No chemistry in components" (non-negotiable 4) is only a convention today. `check:size` and `check:hardcode` already cover `.tsx`, but nothing stops `src/ui`, `src/render` or `src/features` from importing the chem toolkit or the validation rules. Fold a rule into the Q10 dependency-cruiser change: those folders may import `src/chem` and `src/search` types only.

**REVIEW REQUIRED (for the Phase 5 contract decisions).**
1. Q1: option B (an app-level derived-indexes service) instead of the store taking the full engine; its main-thread cost after a hub edit is to be benched in 5.1a.
2. Q3: navigator hub expansion is missing in core and needs a step before 5.5a; the memo rule (rebuild by record kinds, structural sharing, content-keyed downstream memos).
3. Q5: remove `selected` / `focused` from `SceneNode.state`; additive `Scene.truncation` / `notes` / layout engine; `depictionKey` meaning.
4. Q7: the `warmUp` method and `ENGINE_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` (proposed 20,000 ms) for the E4 start-up limit.
5. Q9: derived formulas (`SpeciesCheckResult.formula`, `SearchDocument.derivedFormula`, `SearchSync.refresh` / `adopt`).
6. Q10: the dependency-cruiser and ESLint additions, and `src/features/data-exchange` for import and export.
7. Q11: Radix modal layers, Select and ScrollArea inject a `<style>` element under the CSP; the proposed replacements (non-modal parts plus our own focus trap and scroll lock).
8. Environment: the first `npm run check` of this session ran on battery with Edge open and failed 10 real-thread tests (cold RDKit load over 2 s: chem-worker-threads 7, worker-crash-recovery 1, search-worker-threads 1, compute-import-threads 1; 4 files); after the user plugged in it passed as one command (232 files, 3,728 tests, Vitest 111.8 s). Edge was still open and idle (9 processes). No timeout, test or rule was changed.

### Phase 5 contract decisions (reviewer, 2026-10-02)

Docs only: no source, test, dependency, contract, configuration or benchmark change. The plan review (35443d5, 22b8cc1) is ACCEPTED. Each amendment lands, through CLAUDE.md §7, in the step named; nothing is applied now. Step numbers are the NEW ones (old 5.1b = new 5.1b engines + new 5.1c flows; old 5.1c = new 5.1d). The review entry above keeps the old numbers as history.

- Q1 Option B: app-level `DerivedIndexes` service in `src/app/services` (lazy build, ChangeSets queued and applied on read, one build on replace / remote / gap / a queue over its bound, `current()` never kept past the call). No core change. 5.1a benches the first build, an ordinary-edit apply and a hub-edit apply at the design tier. Phase 9 candidate: derived tables over the store's own core handle.

- Q3 (1) New core step 5.4c "Navigator scale and expansion" before 5.5a; semantics fixed from the step 5.0 fact sheet. (2) Additive `ProjectionDefinition.readsKinds`, proved by a property test; pure `sameProjection` in core/graph; the hook keeps the previous Projection object when equal; memos key on object identity; no content hash. Lands: 5.4c (readsKinds), 5.5a (hook).
- Q4 Self-loop edges stay out of the LayoutRequest; glyph beside the node; the Scene counts them; label overlaps accepted until Phase 8. Lands 5.3.
- Q5 (a) `selected` and `focused` leave `SceneNode.state`; the focus mechanism is decided in 5.7 with evidence. (b)(c)(d) as proposed. (e) `depictionKey` through an injected port `depictionKeyOf(ref)`; `src/render` never imports `src/chem` at run time. (f) Only `Scene.truncation` is added. Lands 5.3.
- Q6 Clean-shutdown marker (writer only) in 5.1a; `requestPersistentStorage` in 5.1c; one plain boot-report line each in 5.1d; a refused `setUiState` is a status. Not in Phase 5: periodic snapshots (Phase 6, step 6.1) and `storageEstimate` (Phase 9).
- Q7 Additive idempotent `warmUp` with `ENGINE_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` = 20,000, sent before the first real call; `onRestart` re-warms only if warmed; `firstCallTimeoutMs` rejected; depiction queue (4 in flight) approved. Lands in step 5.0 (item b).
- Q8 Clock, RNG and schedulers in `src/app` (5.1a); port wiring, `SearchSync.adopt` and the in-process import as a value (5.1b, 5.1c); `LayoutServiceOptions.persist` (5.5b); the stale adapter comment (5.1a).
- Q9 As proposed (`SpeciesCheckResult.formula?`, `derivedFormulaOf`, `DocumentPorts`, `SearchDocument.derivedFormula`, `SearchSync.refresh(ids)`): contract, L4 and sync in 5.1b; UI proof in 5.8.
- Q10 In step 5.0: import and export UI in `src/features/data-exchange`; first-run screen is app shell; palette commands come from a registry that `src/app` fills.

Warm-up is sent before the first real call and the calls wait behind it; `ok: false` is kept (chem: `unavailable` with the message; layout: the fallback layout, `engine_unavailable`; no restart); a warm-up TIMEOUT is an ordinary RPC timeout (restart, counts towards maxRestarts, `gave_up` a status; the gate goes back to cold and the next call tries again); `onRestart` re-warms only if the engine had been warmed. **(c) Navigator fact sheet** (read-only, throw-away script, nothing committed; default limits: 400 nodes, 800 edges; build time = median of 30 builds on an indexed state, ms):
- demo: 27 reactions, 15 hubs, 2 unanchored reactions, 35 candidate edges (34 on real hubs), 25 distinct ordered real-hub pairs, projection 16 nodes / 35 edges / 6 bundles (15 edges bundled, largest 4), truncation null, 0.16 ms.
- initial tier, dense, 60 anchors asked (the generator has only 50 classes, so 50 hubs): 1,000 reactions, 1,502 candidates, 1,026 distinct ordered hub pairs (largest pair 6), projection 50 nodes / 800 edges / 144 bundles (317 edges bundled, largest 5), truncation max_edges, 2.55 ms. Without anchors: 0 hubs, all 1,000 reactions Unanchored on the Unclassified hub, 1,502 candidates, 800 edges, ONE bundle of 800 (a self-loop pair), max_edges, 2.29 ms.
- initial tier, hub_explosion, 50 hubs: 1,000 candidates, 1 hub pair (all 1,000 between the same two hubs), projection 800 edges in ONE bundle of 800, max_edges, 1.87 ms.
- design tier (5,000 reactions), dense, 60 anchored hubs: 7,492 candidates, 1,702 distinct ordered hub pairs (largest pair 752), projection 60 nodes / 800 edges / 115 bundles (475 edges bundled, largest 63), max_edges, 4.71 ms (max 7.7).
- design tier, hub_explosion, 60 anchored hubs: 5,000 candidates, 1 hub pair of 5,000, projection 800 edges in ONE bundle of 800, max_edges, 2.48 ms.
Answers in words. (1) Bundles when edges are cut: `bundleEdges` runs on the ADMITTED edges only, after the cut at maxEdges; edges are admitted in (reaction, outcome, product) ID order, so which pairs survive depends on IDs, not on importance; a pair with one admitted edge is no bundle at all. (2) A bundle does NOT know its full count: `EdgeBundle` is `{ id, from, to, edgeIds }` with the admitted edge IDs only (design/dense: largest bundle 63 against a real pair size of 752). (3) `hidden` on a node is `{ outgoing, incoming }`, the number of DROPPED candidate edges seen from that admitted node (an edge dropped by maxEdges is counted at both admitted ends, one dropped edge adds 1 to each; an edge to an unadmitted hub counts only at the admitted end); the sum over nodes is 2 x dropped (design/dense 13,384 = 2 x (7,492 - 800)); it says nothing per hub pair and is not capped to a pair. (4) The roll-up index answers, without materialising edges (no `toEdge`, no hashing): per hub, `candidatesFrom(hub)` and `candidatesTo(hub)` (sorted lists whose lengths are the unfiltered outgoing and incoming counts) and the unanchored reaction list; per hub pair there is NO index, a count is a scan of one hub's list filtered on the other hub (the cost of that list, up to 5,000 in hub_explosion); filters (topic, scope, text) are applied per reaction in `build`, so the roll-up's counts are unfiltered upper bounds unless the caller filters the candidates itself.
