Same build and harness rules as part 1 (production build on 4173; a NON-MINIFIED temp build on 4174 for function names; headless Chromium 153, Windows 11; nothing in `src/` changed; no budget, threshold, run count or timeout changed). New harnesses (informal, `tests/measure/`): `import-profile.measure.ts` (V8 CPU profile of the main thread over preview and apply; self and inclusive time), `import-conflict.measure.ts` (conflicting preview, send / receive costs), `boot-phases.measure.ts` (worker calls, IndexedDB transactions and a CPU profile through boot); the first two take `ORN_BY_PATH=1`. MACHINE NOTE: for the first runs of this session the CPU was throttled (a fixed 3e8-iteration Node loop took 2,105 ms; about 1.9 GHz under load; boot 7.3 s against 2.1 s). The user was asked, the machine was restored (the same loop 893 ms) and every figure below was taken AFTER that, with the loop re-run between runs (885-898 ms). The throttled runs are discarded. Reference for the reviewer: that loop = about 0.9 s on this machine at full speed.

a. The 3,707 ms preview task (5.9a). CAUSE, PROVEN: it is the HARNESS, not the app. Self time of the whole window sits in an anonymous function with no URL (`:7578`) under `setInputFiles` (Playwright's injected script: the 16.9 MB buffer is sent through the protocol as base64, `atob`, then rebuilt into a `File` on the page's main thread). Uploading the same bytes BY PATH (the browser reads the file natively): the preview window is 2,435 ms with NO long task and the main thread 95% idle (the parse and preview run in the compute worker). Buffer upload: task 1,531 ms here (3,323 ms in an earlier, throttled run). Top 5 self time inside that task (buffer upload): (anonymous) Playwright injected script 966 ms; (program) 395 ms; (garbage collector) 51 ms; (anonymous) injected script 35 ms; `atob` 27 ms. Top by self time inside the app during a path upload: nothing over 30 ms (React render 28 ms, `hashOf` 19 ms, `digest` 18 ms). Remedy: none needed in the product; the e2e kit's `chooseFile` should upload large files by path (a harness change, proposed, not made). The 5.9a figure and the buffer-upload conflict-preview figure both include this.

b. The 2,644 ms apply block (5.9a). It is the app. Figures at full speed: the apply window is 3.2 s from the click; the main thread has 3 long tasks (99, 849 and 90 ms); the longest, 849 ms, is `run` (import flow) -> `store.replaceState` (473 ms inclusive) + the persistence write. CAUSE, PROVEN by the profile (non-minified): inside the 849 ms task, top 5 by self time: `put` (native IndexedDB structured clone inside Dexie's bulk write) 175 ms; Dexie `mutate` closure (`index:50781`) 133 ms; (garbage collector) 56 ms; `postMessage` of the whole state to the compute worker 56 ms; `matchPath.visit` (reference extraction while the store builds its indexes, `addRecord` -> `append`) 47 ms. By inclusive time: the Dexie write of all records 308 ms, the store's own `replaceState` 473 ms (immer `freeze`, core index build, `addRecord`) and sending the state to the worker. The 2,644 ms / 1,091 ms of 5.9a did not reproduce at full speed (849 ms); I cannot say whether 5.9a was throttled or measured something else, so the 5.9a figure is not used. Proposed remedy (not built): write the records in slices that yield to the event loop (the 17,101 records in chunks of a few thousand per transaction), or move the write to the worker that already holds the state; the structured clone itself is native and cannot be made cheaper.

c. Conflicting hub_explosion import preview (design tier, 15.8 MB, 17,101 records, every ID conflicting): file chosen to preview 1,527 / 1,516 ms uploaded by path (row: 5,000 ms: INSIDE); 3,072 ms as a buffer (harness cost of a). First import into an empty store: preview 1,455 ms, Confirm to "Imported" 2,085 ms. Worker calls over 5 ms on the main thread: `loadReplica` postMessage 49-51 ms; search `load` 10 ms; message handling over 20 ms: 87, 30, 23 ms. The one long task of the apply is 753 ms (replaceState). The file held the same records, so the preview says "0 would be written"; a file with different records under the same IDs was not measured (REVIEW REQUIRED 3).

d. Boot phase breakdown, Chromium, design tier, 3 cold + 3 warm timelines (production build; ms from navigation start) and 2 cold + 2 warm CPU profiles (non-minified):
| phase | at (cold) | what the main thread is doing |
|---|---|---|
| open database | 199 -> 270 (warm 219 -> 238) | idle (IndexedDB open) |
| read the committed state (`records` + `meta` transaction) | 277 -> 472 (195 ms) | idle |
| assemble the state, zod `parse` of every record | 472 -> about 690 | busy, 150-220 ms (`assembleState`, `safeParse`) |
| send the state to the compute worker | `loadReplica` sent 688 | 49-57 ms to serialise |
| compute worker: deserialise, validate, findings (`loadReplica` answered) | 688 -> 1,591 (903 ms; warm 888 ms) | IDLE for about 0.9 s (profile buckets 750-1,500 ms hold 0-6 ms) |
| create the canonical store: `build` indexes, `addRecord` | 1,621 -> about 1,800 | busy, 165-250 ms |
| quarantine count read | 1,603 -> 1,834 (231 ms) | idle; the status turns "ready" only after it (ready 1,804) |
| overview projection: `buildProjection`, layout request | 1,867 -> 2,050 | busy, 165-180 ms |
| search: derived-cache reads, `worker-search.load` | 1,777 -> 2,166 (load 101 ms; `load` 81 ms on main) | busy about 80 ms |
| first overview drawn | 2,101 cold / 2,071 warm; all 6 runs 2,071-2,165 | |

The cold / warm gap is 0-60 ms: neither the HTTP cache nor the code cache is where the time goes. WARM 2,071-2,092 ms is 570-590 ms over the 1.5 s row; cold is inside 2.5 s. Evidence for a remedy, by the size of the wait: (1) the main thread is idle for about 0.9 s while the compute worker validates (`loadReplica`); the store needs its findings (`precomputed`), so the order is a dependency of the design, not an accident; the worker-side split (deserialise / validate / index) was not profiled (the main-thread profile does not see the worker): LIKELY validation and index build, to be proved before a remedy; (2) the quarantine read (231 ms) and the derived-cache reads run after the worker answers, not beside it: they could start at the same time as `loadReplica` (LIKELY 200+ ms); (3) the zod parse of every stored record on the main thread (150-220 ms) runs before the send. Nothing was built or tried.

e. Phase-4-close §9 items re-measured here (the bench-based rows 1, 2 (in-process half), 5, 6, 9 follow in part 3): 1: main-thread cost of moving a whole state, in the browser at the design tier: send 49-57 ms (row: 57 / 190 ms), merged state back 87 ms (first message-handling event of the apply); 2: restore through the worker, whole `loadReplica` round trip 888-903 ms in the browser (3.3 s in 4.2d), main thread idle for all of it; 3: search documents on the main thread: `load` 81 ms inclusive in the profile, `worker-search.load` 101 ms round trip (193 ms in 4.5); 4: item c, 1,516-1,527 ms against 5,000 ms; 7: a restarted chem thread: the WASM `warmUp` `loadMs` is 83-97 ms in four measurements (cold and warm HTTP cache), the call limit is 2 s: more than 20 times inside. Apply latency (openItem 34, prepare + validate twice, 1.4-2.3 s): Confirm to "Imported" 2,085-2,155 ms (design dense and hub_explosion), unchanged by this session.

Honest limits: headless, software rendering, one machine whose speed changed during the session (see MACHINE NOTE); profiles at 1 ms sampling slow the page by about 10-15%; profile times start at the profiler start, a few tens of ms before navigation.

### Phase 5, step 5.10b, part 2W - WebKit import stall, diagnosis (2026-10-13)

Diagnosis only; nothing in `src/` changed; production build on 4173; Playwright's WebKit on Windows (NOT Safari: a different port). Harnesses (informal, `tests/measure/`): `webkit-stall.measure.ts` (generated 'initial'-dense file scaled to a size, uploaded by path; records every worker request / answer, every IndexedDB transaction and its end, page and worker errors, the dialog text), `webkit-idb-raw.measure.ts` (raw IndexedDB puts, none of the app's code). The part-1 reading "stall" is WRONG: the import is not stuck, it is very slow, and part 1 stopped waiting too early.

a. Threshold: there is none; the time is linear in the number of records. Persistent context, time from Confirm to "Imported": 0.5 MB (512 records) 10 s; 2 MB (2,050 records) 35 s; 3.5 MB (3,584 records) 60 s; 16.9 MB (17,283 records) 276 s (part 1 waited 300 s from the file chosen and saw no end: the apply ends at about 280 s after a 16-20 s preview). That is about 15.5 ms per record. Chromium, same files: about 1 s for 3.5 MB (5 s is the poll step of the harness). A WebKit context that is NOT persistent (the default of `browser.newContext`) opens the app in session-only mode ("Applied N records ... not saved") and ends at once: that is what the e2e suite exercises, which is LIKELY why the e2e suite passed (not checked against its config).

b. Where it stops: nowhere. Last worker request: `adoptPending` / second `loadReplica`, all answered (ok=true, 100-2,300 ms). The one IndexedDB transaction that matters, `readwrite [records, meta, assetBlobs]` (the apply's write), COMPLETED after 31.7 s (2 MB), 55.5 s (3.5 MB), 270.5 s (16.9 MB); `derivedCache` writes wait behind it. No transaction aborted except the boot `snapshots` probe (the same in Chromium), no error or QuotaExceeded on the page or in a worker (Chromium: same file, same sequence, transaction under 1 s). The page stays responsive (heartbeat every 500 ms kept time: 539 beats in 278 s), the web process is idle: the browser's IndexedDB backend is the wait.

c. Does the UI give up? No. "Applying the records... This step can no longer be cancelled; it will finish and then say so." stays on screen for the whole wait: no timeout, no progress figure, no error, no banner. It is not a silent failure (the text says what is happening and the import ends with the normal "Imported" notice), but a user sees 4.5 minutes of an unchanging message and no way to leave; that is a usability finding for the reviewer.

d. Warm boot in WebKit (2.5x cold): NOT traced (time-box; the stop request of the session).

e. Cause, PROVEN (raw IndexedDB, no app code, persistent WebKit): N puts of 1 KB in ONE transaction: 200 puts 3,126 ms, 2,000 puts 30,803 ms, 5,000 puts 77,200 ms (15.4 ms per put, linear); ONE put of a 2 MB value 25 ms; Chromium: 10 / 88 / 244 ms and 23 ms. So in this WebKit build the cost is PER put REQUEST (about 15 ms each), not per byte. The app writes one object-store record per canonical record (17,000 puts). Whether real Safari (macOS, iOS) behaves like Playwright's Windows WebKit is UNKNOWN: this is a WebKit-only finding that needs a check on real Safari before release (reviewer decision 4). If Safari shows it, the smallest fix I would propose (its own step after Gate E, not built): write records to IndexedDB in fewer, larger values (pages of a few hundred records per put, behind the persistence adapter; schema and migration step, so the amendment procedure applies), plus a progress line ("saved 4,000 of 17,283") so the wait is not mute. If Safari is fast, it is a harness limit and only the progress line is worth keeping. Same cause LIKELY (not tested) for the WebKit warm boot (state read at 1.4 s against 0.3 s: reading is per-record too) and for the part-1 failure to seed the design tier.

Honest limits: one machine (CPU at full speed, reference loop 0.9 s), headless; WebKit runs were one each per size; the 16.9 MB file is the 'initial' tier scaled, not the design-tier file of part 1 (same order of records, 17,283 against 17,101 in hub_explosion).

### Phase 5, step 5.11a, part 1 - WebKit waits (2026-10-14)

Causes (found by reading the code; the failure was not reproduced before the fix, the packet saw it 1 time in 2 + 3 runs):
- arrows.spec.ts:131 "expected 1 React commit, saw 0": the counter `data-layer-commits` is bumped by `useCommitProbe`, a passive `useEffect` (src/render/svg/use-commit-probe.ts). Passive effects run after paint, so the overlay can be in the DOM (what the test waited for with `toHaveCount`) before its commit is counted; the test read the counter at once and could see the old value. The probe is not wrong (it counts commits); the wait was.
- csp.spec.ts:95 "no eval violation seen": the `securitypolicyviolation` event is queued by the engine as a task. `addScriptTag` resolves on the script's load, and the test read the collected list straight after it; in WebKit the event can be delivered after that read. The `watch` listener was registered early enough; the read was not awaited on the event.

Changed tests (intent kept; no budget, threshold, run count or timeout changed):
1. arrows.spec.ts "a hovered arrow is drawn by the overlay...": after the overlay is visible, `expect.poll` waits until the commit count has moved past its value before the hover, then the count must be exactly 1 (as written before). No sleep. Reason: the probe is a passive effect (above).
2. csp.spec.ts "eval and new Function...": a listener is registered in the page BEFORE the probe script runs and resolves a promise at the first script-src violation whose blockedURI contains "eval"; the test awaits that promise (the event resolves it), then keeps its old assertions. Reason: the event arrives after the script's load (above).

Proof: both specs with `--repeat-each=20` in WebKit: 40 passed (3.2 min); once in Chromium and once in Firefox: 4 passed.

### Phase 5, step 5.11b, part 1 - apply progress (2026-10-14)

What was built:
- Writer (`src/persistence/write-slices.ts`, `adapter.ts` `persist`): the record puts of the ONE `rw` transaction are made as slices of 32 rows. All slice `bulkPut` calls are issued at once, in order; a report `{ written, total }` is made when each slice's writes succeed (before the commit). A failing slice rejects the group and the error leaves the transaction: nothing is committed (INV-20, INV-21 unchanged). `adapter.watchWriteProgress(listener)` is how the app listens.
- Flow (`import-service.ts`): during an apply the reports go into `AppStatus.operation.progress` (done, total) and the listener is removed in `finally`.
- Model (`apply-pace.ts`, `import-model.ts`): under 2 s nothing extra is kept in the state; after 2 s `long` is true and the newest count is shown at most 4 times a second (250 ms gap, the newest value waits for its turn); a count only rises (a retried write or a new stage's null does not take it back); at the end the final count is shown at once. The clock is injected (`PaceClock`).
- Screen (`import-screen.tsx`): once long and the writer has reported, "Applying the records... N of M" and a `role="progressbar"` (aria-valuemin 0, aria-valuemax M, aria-valuenow N) sit OUTSIDE the live region; the live region (role="status") holds the file line, the stage and, from the start of the long wait, "Keep this tab open until it finishes."; the result is announced by the existing toast. So the live region changes at the start of the long wait and at the end, never per update. No Cancel button in the long view once the commit has begun (decision, see Amendments; an openItem for Phase 6 to revisit). Before the writer reports (a long preparing/snapshot stage) the old stage line and the Cancel that still changes nothing stay.
- A failure in the middle: the write queue keeps the failed batch and retries as before; the flow answers with the SaveStatus, so the dialog closes with the existing "not saved yet (message)" warning, or the refusal view for a refused apply; never "Imported". Tested: a fault after two slices leaves records and meta empty.

Slice size, from measurement (Chromium 153, production build, design-tier dense file 16.9 MB uploaded by path, Confirm to "Imported"; speed check 590-620 ms for the 3e8 loop in every session):
| writer | Confirm to Imported (ms) |
|---|---|
| BEFORE (one `bulkPut` of all rows), two sessions of 3 runs | 1,667 / 1,660 / 1,680 (mean 1,667) and 1,667 / 1,636 / 1,663 (mean 1,655) |
| slices waited for one by one, 32 / 128 / 512 puts | 1,921 / 1,931 / 1,933 (+16%) |
| waited one by one, 2,048 or 9,000 or 100,000 puts | 1,440 / 1,573 / 1,659 |
| waited one by one, size ramped 32 -> 128 -> 512 -> 2,048 | 1,917 (+15%) |
| ISSUED at once, 32 puts (built), 3 runs | 1,679 / 1,699 / 1,717 (mean 1,698: +1.9% against 1,667, +2.6% against 1,655) |
Reading: waiting for a slice before issuing the next costs Chromium +15 to +16% for any first slice under about 1,000 puts (in a timeline the last write ended at the same time in both; the extra 500 ms came after it, in main-thread work that, with a large first slice, had run between the slices instead). I did not find the exact cause and did not need to: issuing every slice at once, as the single `bulkPut` did, costs +2%, and then the slice size only sets how often progress is heard. 32 puts, because Playwright's WebKit pays about 15.5 ms per put (PROGRESS 5.10b part 2W): a slice is then about 0.5 s, so a report arrives about twice a second there; Chromium reports a slice in about 1 ms and the model shows at most 4 a second. The Chromium apply is NOT more than 10% slower, so there is no stop. (Two designs were built and measured on the way to this one: slices waited for one by one, with a fixed size, and with a size grown from the injected clock; both are gone.)

Tests: unit `src/persistence/write-slices.test.ts` (3) and `src/features/data-exchange/apply-pace.test.ts` (7: the 2 s threshold, the 4-a-second rate, a steady writer seen at least once a second, only rises, N equals M at the end, a new start forgets); integration `tests/integration/persistence-write-progress.test.ts` (4: slices and values in ONE transaction, a throwing listener, a mid-way fault commits nothing and the same write lands whole once the fault is cleared) and one test in `tests/integration/app-services-flows-guards.test.ts` (operation.progress rises to the total, then null); component `src/features/data-exchange/import-screen-progress.test.tsx` (7: nothing under 2 s, the bar and its ARIA values, the texts, no Cancel, the live region never carries the count, a failed apply is never "Imported"); e2e `tests/e2e/apply-progress.spec.ts` (WebKit 0.5 MB: 96, 128, 160 ... 512 in steps of 32, aria-valuemax 512, axe 18 rules 0 problems, then "Imported"; Chromium: the demo import shows no progress view and ends in "Imported"). `Faults.failAfter` was added to `src/test-support/persistence-kit.ts` (a fault in the middle of a transaction). No existing test was changed or weakened. `npm run check`: 392 test files, 5478 tests passed.

### Release preview, fix - names on the phone first view (2026-10-14)

Cause (REVIEW REQUIRED 1 of part 3, confirmed from the phone screenshots): Fit and the first view floored at the bare LOD 1 threshold 0.35, and `lodWithHysteresis` needs 0.35 x 1.05 = 0.3675 to rise from LOD 0, so the phone showed LOD 0: blank family boxes. Fix: `FIT_FLOOR` in `transform.ts` = LOD_THRESHOLDS[1] x (1 + LOD_HYSTERESIS) + 0.01 margin (0.3775), derived from the constants; Fit and the first view use it. Wider screens whose Fit is above the floor are unchanged. Tests: `transform.test.ts` (+1: the floor is above the entry point with hysteresis and gives LOD >= 1 from LOD 0; the bare threshold does not; the three floor-value assertions now use `FIT_FLOOR`); `phone.spec.ts`: after Load demo dataset data-lod is not 0 and the family name "Alcohols" is visible, both devices. `npm run check` green (394 files, 5,500 tests); full e2e Chromium 120 passed, 5 skipped; phone.spec WebKit passed.

### Phone mode, part 1 - load measurement (2026-10-16)

Measured against the LIVE URL (https://reaction-navigator.organic-reaction-navigator.workers.dev, from PROJECT_STATE releasePreview, commit 81bf4e8, nothing changed in `src/`). `tests/measure/phone-load.measure.ts`: Chromium 153.0.8010.12 (Playwright), Pixel 7 profile, CDP: CPU slowdown 4x on the PAGE (workers' CPU not slowed; with it slowed the result below was the same), network 1.6 Mbps down / 750 kbps up / 150 ms latency on the page and on each worker session, a NEW profile per run (cache empty), 5 runs; visit 2 keeps the HTTP cache and clears IndexedDB (the demo is loaded again). Times are ms since navigation start; medians, (min-max). The dev machine is fast and the origin is Cloudflare (cf HIT on every asset); the numbers are the throttle's.

| | cold (visit 1) | warm cache (visit 2, "d") |
|---|---|---|
| (a) navigation -> "Get started" visible | 3083 (2992-4189) | 834 (785-1182) |
| (b) "Load demo dataset" -> first view drawn | 2499 (2009-2914) | 728 (696-1504) |
| chem engine reported "ok" (since navigation) | 5135 (4959-6089) | 2029 (1737-2496) |
| (c) Alcohols family page -> first structure, opened as a visitor does (as soon as the map is drawn) | NEVER within 60 s, 0 of 5 runs | 299 (202-316), page shown 179 |
| (c') the same, reopened after the wasm had loaded | 352 (335-403), 5 of 5 | - |

Per resource, cold run 3 (start / end ms since navigation; transfer bytes / decoded bytes; encoding; all `cf-cache-status: HIT`; "-" = not compressed by the server, they are woff/woff2 already): `/` 0-407, 1,286 / 826, zstd; `index-*.js` 411-2627, 397,007 / 1,195,197, zstd (the biggest on the critical path); `index-*.css` 412-664, 8,990 / 38,693; compute worker script requested at 2879; two fonts (sans 400, 600) 3113-4031, 23-25 kB each, "-"; search worker 3288; `demo.orn-*.json` 3322-4314, 27,108 / (333,492 on disk), zstd; import screen chunks (js, module, css) 4345-4626, 6,126 + 1,210 + 1,639; mono font 4860-5623, 15,551; chem worker script requested 5236; layout worker 5678; RDKit glue (in the chem worker) 6007-6638, 24,372 / 63,765; `RDKit_minimal-*.wasm` 6642-18982, 2,318,206 / 7,333,095, zstd (12.3 s of the line on its own). Warm run 3: every asset comes from the disk cache (0 bytes transfer; only `/` revalidates, 832 B), the wasm is read in 81 ms (1874-1955), first view at 1763.
Long tasks (main thread, run 3): cold 6 tasks, 704 ms in all, 404 ms over the 50 ms mark, the longest 269 ms at 2628 (parsing and running the 1.2 MB `index` script); warm 6 tasks, 760 ms, longest 328 ms at 311. The page's own work is not the wait; the bytes are.
When things load (cold, run 3): compute worker 2.9 s, search worker 3.3 s, chem worker 5.2 s (it is started at its first need, after the demo is imported), layout worker 5.7 s, RDKit glue 6.0 s, RDKit wasm 6.6 to 19.0 s. Compression: `.js`, `.wasm`, `.json` and `.css` are all served compressed (Chromium negotiates zstd; curl with `Accept-Encoding: br` gets `br`; `gzip` is the fallback); fonts are not (already compressed formats); `/` too.

FINDING (REVIEW REQUIRED, a real bug, not a measure artefact): on a slow phone a family page opened right after the demo loads NEVER draws its structures. The page opens at about 7-9 s; RDKit is ready at 19 s. The structure requests made before that fail, the retry hook gives up after `MAX_DEPICTION_RETRIES` = 3 at 250 ms steps (`use-depiction-retry.ts`), the engine never reports "unavailable", so the "engine came back" path (`recovered`) never re-asks, and the cards stay on their formulas ("The structure could not be drawn" title) until the visitor leaves and reopens the page (c': 352 ms). On a fast desktop RDKit is ready in about a second, so the race is invisible. Not fixed here (part 1 changes nothing in `src/`).

Top 3 fixes, with what each should save (estimates from the table; the reviewer decides in the next prompt):
1. Re-ask for structures when the engine becomes ready (the bug above): cold first family page from "never" to about (RDKit ready - page opened) + 0.35 s, i.e. structures appear on their own about 10 s after the page opens on this throttle, instead of needing a manual reopen. Small, in the depiction manager / retry hook (a "chem ready" signal re-requests every key that failed for `not ready`).
2. Start the RDKit wasm download at page load (a `<link rel="preload" as="fetch" crossorigin>` of the wasm, or boot the chem worker right after the first paint) instead of at the first need (5.2 s for the worker, 6.6 s for the wasm): the wasm then shares the line with `index.js` from about 0.4 s. Bytes on the line are the same (2.7 MB, so at least 13.5 s at 1.6 Mbps), so RDKit ready moves from 19.0 s to about 14-15 s (about 4-5 s earlier), and the family page opened at 7-9 s waits less. Costs 2.3 MB for a visitor who never draws a structure.
3. Send fewer bytes: the wasm as pre-compressed brotli at quality 11 is 1,703,694 B against 2,318,206 B served now (-614 kB, about 3 s at 1.6 Mbps); `index.js` 327,005 B against 397,007 B (-70 kB, about 0.35 s). Needs the host to serve pre-built `.br` files (to be checked for Workers static assets) or the build to emit them. A smaller win after that: split `index.js` so the first-run screen loads less than 1.2 MB of script (not measured; 0.5-1 s at best).
Raw per-run data (per-resource lists for all 10 visits): kept out of the repo (a 1 MB JSON); re-run `npx tsx tests/measure/phone-load.measure.ts 5 <url> out.json` to regenerate it.

### Phone mode, part 3 - bottom sheet inspector (2026-10-16)

### Phone mode A review (reviewer, 2026-10-16)

Verdict: ACCEPTED. Approved as built: ADR-039, the shell, More, the alert line, folded notices, the bottom sheet, the Families / Map / Search tabs, the floating Fit and Legend, the name floor, the measurement harness, every changed test.
REVIEW REQUIRED items, answered: (1) the structures bug: fixed in Phone mode B, part 1. (2) The 0.01 px tolerance in shell.spec: accepted (float rounding of layout units, not a smaller target). (3) Phone CSS keyed on data-layout from the one hook: accepted, better than a second copy of the queries; ADR-039 reworded to say so. ### Phone mode B, part 1 - load fixes (2026-10-16)

Start: HEAD 4bf212a, tree clean, ports 4173 / 4174 / 8787 free. Part A (review recorded) is its own commit, "phone-mode: A review recorded".

(a) THE BUG, fixed. A structure request that failed because the chem engine was not READY yet is asked again, once, when the engine becomes ready, for every consumer (family cards, inspector, mechanism rows: all use the one binding and `useRetryingDepiction`). How: the depiction manager takes an optional `isPending()` (the binding passes `port.enginePending()`: the chem engine is `cold` or `loading`); a failure (an answer, a rejection or the 8 s timeout) that comes while it is pending is kept as `unavailable` with the reason `not_ready` (`DEPICTION_NOT_READY`); `forgetNotReady()` forgets exactly those keys and tells their listeners, so the hook sees `idle` and asks again (250 ms, its existing bounded retry). A failure for any other reason is not touched. The navigator port implements `enginePending` and `engineReady` (every move of the engine status to `ready`); the binding listens to `engineReady` only after a request was made while the engine was loading and drops the listener when it fires (a binding that never asked early listens to nothing; the inspector makes one binding per drawing). `drawingFailed(status)` (new, `src/render/svg`) is what the cards use for the "could not be drawn" look: a `not_ready` key still reads "Drawing the structure..." with its name and formula, no error title.
Tests (unit): `depictions.test.ts` (+3: pending failure -> not_ready for an answer, a timeout and a rejection, forgetNotReady forgets exactly those and tells listeners; another reason is kept; a drawing stays a drawing, nothing after dispose), `use-depiction-retry.test.tsx` (+2: two cards share one re-ask after not ready -> ready and then show the drawing; a failure for another reason is not asked again), `features/navigator/depictions.test.ts` (+1, the binding end to end), `navigator-port.test.ts` (+2: enginePending by state, engineReady at every move to ready and after unsubscribing), `family-structure.test.tsx` (new, 3: the card keeps name and formula and says "Drawing the structure..." without the error title; it draws by itself when the engine is ready; an ordinary failure keeps the error look). e2e `structures-late.spec.ts` (Chromium; the wasm request is held 14 s by `context.route`, longer than the 8 s manager timeout): Alcohols opened right after "Load demo dataset": the card says "Drawing the structure..." with no error title, then the structure appears with no reopening (16 s); with `enginePending` forced to false the same test FAILS (1.5 min timeout), so it does catch the bug.

(b) NOT DONE, on the reviewer's decision. The idle start of the chem worker was built and measured and made (b) slower, so it was removed again (nothing of it is in the commit): see the table. The reviewer chose "drop 1b, keep 1a". The wasm is 2.7 MB on a line of 1.6 Mbps (13.5 s at least); starting it earlier only made it share the line with the demo's own files.

(c) Measurement. `tests/measure/phone-load.measure.ts`, Chromium 153, Pixel 7 profile, CPU 4x on the page, network 1.6 Mbps / 750 kbps / 150 ms on the page and on each worker, a NEW profile per run, 5 runs, medians (ms since the action; min-max in the files). ### Phone mode C, part 4 - the WebKit canvas-keyboard flake (2026-10-16)

Failing test: `canvas-keyboard.spec.ts` "Enter shows the family in the inspector; Enter again opens its page; ..." (WebKit; announcement "Zoom 61 percent" where "Opened the family page of Aldehydes" is expected). Reproduced: 3 of 20 on 62b158a in WebKit.
CAUSE (found with a throw-away copy of the spec that logged the live region, the key events and the viewport, and temporary logging in `ViewportScene` / `onSettled`; all removed): the first Enter selects Aldehydes, the inspector opens, the map gets narrower, and `measure()` fits the map again (the automatic re-fit that follows the drawing's size, step 5.10a). A fit is commanded in the controller at once but drawn, and so stored, on the next frame. When the second Enter opens the family page the map unmounts and its cleanup flushes the pending report of the view: `settle()` reported the STORE's view (0.613, the last drawn frame) and compared it with `autoView`, the CONTROLLER's newest automatic fit (0.465). They differ, so the report said "not automatic" and the canvas announced "Zoom 61 percent" as if the person had zoomed (the 67 -> 61 percent difference of the earlier fit and this one), 3 ms after the Enter, over "Opened the family page of Aldehydes". Not a focus trail or a test timing problem: a product bug that the page's timing made visible (the size change and the unmount fall in the same frame).
FIX (product, `src/render/viewport/viewport-scene.tsx`): the drawing remembers the views of its latest automatic fits (`autoViews`, at most `MAX_AUTO_VIEWS` = 8) and a report is automatic when the view equals any of them; `autoView` still decides whether a size change fits again. No test weakened, no wait added.
Test first: `viewport-scene.test.tsx` (+1): a drawing that goes away while an automatic fit is waiting for its frame reports the view as automatic (it FAILED before the fix with [true, false]); the existing "says whether the settled view is still the automatic one" still passes ([true, true, false]).
Proof: `--repeat-each=20` in WebKit: 20 of 20 passed (before the fix: 3 of 20 failed); once in Chromium and once in Firefox: passed.
Changed existing tests: none.

### Step 6.1a, part 2 - editor sessions core (2026-10-17)

New pure module `src/core/editing/` (`contracts.ts`, `session.ts`, `conflict.ts`, `commit.ts`, `index.ts`; imports only core and immer; clock and IDs through `CommandContext`; no dependency-rule change). ADR-040 "Editor sessions" and a note in UI_ARCHITECTURE section 7 written; Amendments entry (see below).
- `openSession(ctx, state, revision, target | { kind })`: `eds_` ID; `baseRecord` and `draft` are copies; a new record starts as `{ kind, id }` (a fresh ID with the kind's prefix; the schema still decides whether it is a record). A missing target is `{ ok: false, reason: 'not_found' }`.
- `editDraft(session, recipe, ctx, meta?)`: `produceWithPatches`; inverse patches on `past`, `future` cleared, `updatedAt` set; an edit that changes nothing returns the same session. Coalescing: same `meta.path` within 1,000 ms (inclusive) of the previous edit joins the previous step (the combined step is the new inverse followed by the previous one); the path and time live in a WeakMap keyed by the session value (memory only). At most 200 steps, oldest dropped first.
- `undoDraft` / `redoDraft`: exact; the patches that undo an application are the ones Immer produces for it.
- `compareForConflict(base, current, draft)`: per field path (top level and one level into plain objects), base / theirs / mine and `same | theirsOnly | mineOnly | both`; both sides changing a field to the same value is `same`. Compared by `canonicalJson`, which MOVED to `src/core/text/canonical-json.ts` (core may not import `io`); `src/io/canonical-json.ts` re-exports it, so no io import changed.
- `commitDraft(store, session, ctx, choices?, { section })`: L1 first (`parseRecord`; its findings already carry field paths in the Finding shape, so nothing new was needed) -> `invalid`; then the conflict check -> `conflict` unless `choices` resolve every `both` field (the target deleted: `conflict` with `current: null`, whatever the choices; an ID clash on create is a `conflict` too); the merged record is parsed again; ONE `dispatch` labelled "Edit <section> of <name>" (name of the stored record before the edit, else its ID), `expectedRevision` the store's revision at that moment, `selectionHint` the record. `VALIDATION_FAILED` -> `invalid` with its findings. Provenance times: the existing builders set none on an update, so none are set.
Amendment (additive): `DraftCommitOutcome` gains `reason: 'refused'` with the store's `CommandError` for every refusal that is not about the draft (READ_ONLY, and EMPTY_COMMAND when nothing would change, for example after choosing "theirs" everywhere). Recorded under Amendments.
Tests first for each function (the module's tests were written together with the code and run before the commit): `session.test.ts` (open, edit, coalescing with the injected clock including the exact 1,000 ms edge and "memory only" after a JSON round trip, the 200-step bound, a property test: undoing every step returns each earlier draft in turn and redoing all returns the final one), `conflict.test.ts` (all four statuses, absent vs empty, key order, new record), `commit.test.ts` (one global entry however many local edits, label, undo, another record changing is no conflict, create, L1 refused with field path, an L3 ERROR (REF-001) refused with the store untouched, read-only refused, conflict choices mine / theirs, deleted target, nothing to save, a property test: a commit after any edit sequence equals the final draft in the store, as one history entry). `npm run check` green: 410 files, 5,636 tests.
Changed existing tests: none (`canonical-json.test.ts` moved with its file, content unchanged).

### Equation step, part 3 - fact sheet and RDKit spike (2026-10-17)

NO product code. The spike was a throw-away script outside the repo (deleted: nothing under `src/` or `tests/` changed). All line numbers are of HEAD ca58758.
(a) How "Show full equation" is built today
- `EquationTerm` (`src/core/graph/full-equation.ts:17-30`): `coefficient` (string or null; null when absent or 1, `:42`), `name` (the participant's `originalText`, else the described record's name, else its ID, `:59-63`), `word` (the selectivity word, set on ONE main product, the last, `:85`), `quantifier` ("both" / "all" on that term, `:80,86`), `role` ("coproduct" / "byproduct" for a non-main product, `:87`), `text` (the term as one line, `:50-51`). There is NO reference to the record behind a term (no species ID, no structure): a term is name and words only.
- Which participants become terms: reactants = `reaction.participants` with `role === 'reactant'` that apply under the outcome's condition variants (`appliesTo`, `:64-65`); products = every `outcome.products` entry of the chosen outcome, main or not (`:81`). Reagents, catalysts, solvents and conditions are NOT terms: they go to `FullEquation.arrow` (`arrowTextOf`, `:99-108`: reagents `above`, conditions `below`, stage numbers inside the parts; a species already written on the left is omitted by ref and by formula, `:97-108`). `FullEquation.text` = "reactants -> products" without arrow text (`:115`).
- Stages: only through the arrow parts (a `separator` part carries the stage number; `partsToRuns`, `src/render/scene/formatted-text.ts:177-185`); coefficients: `Participant.coefficient` / product `coefficient`, printed "2 Benzaldehyde" in `text`.
- Reversibility: the schema has it, `Reaction.reversibility.kind` in `equilibrium | reversible_under_other_conditions | irreversible | unknown` (`src/core/schema/reaction.ts:200,233`). Neither the card nor the equation reads it: they draw ONE arrow always (`EquationArrow`, `src/ui/primitives/equation-arrow.tsx`; the card's `Arrow` / `DownArrow`). Only the inspector's L2 facts print it as words (`src/features/inspector/view-reaction.tsx:161`). `FullEquation` carries no reversibility.
- Formula typography helper: YES, `formulaRuns(text, charge?)` (`src/render/scene/formatted-text.ts:139-172`): digits after an element symbol or a closing bracket are subscript runs, a trailing charge is a superscript run (the record's `charge` decides when given; a bare "NH4+" is left plain because digits then a sign are ambiguous, `tailOf` `:107-129`), everything else plain; the runs joined equal the input. `partsToRuns` (`:177`) uses it for arrow parts. It is typography only. R, R' and X are not special-cased (they are plain letters).
- Where the equation is printed: (1) the family card, desktop AND phone: `OutcomeRow` renders `FullEquationView` under every outcome (`src/features/navigator/family-card.tsx:89`; the phone differs only in the scheme above it, `:72-79`), `src/features/navigator/family-equation.tsx:12-27` (a `<details>`; one `<p aria-label="Full equation: <text>">`: reactant names joined by " + ", `EquationArrow`, product names); (2) the inspector's reaction view: `FullEquations` (`src/features/inspector/view-reaction.tsx:149` -> `src/features/inspector/equation.tsx:34-56`; a `<ul aria-label="Full equation">`, one `<li aria-label="<label>: <text>">` per outcome). The data come from `fullEquationOf` through the family study (`src/core/graph/family/study.ts:159`) and `fullEquationsOfReaction` (inspector). Both print term text as plain names: no drawings, no formulas.
(b) The chem worker today
- `StructureFacts` (`src/chem/contracts.ts:23-36`): `canonicalSmiles`, `formula` (Hill, `src/chem/rdkit/facts.ts:53-68`), `charge`, `heavyAtomCount` (`mol.get_num_atoms(true)`, `facts.ts:113,126`), stereo counts, `hasDoubleBondStereo`, `cipCounts`, `aromatic` (a boolean), `atomMaps`, `warnings`. **Heavy-atom count: yes. Ring count: NO field today** (only `aromatic`). RDKit gives it (spike below), so it is an additive fact: `ringCount` (REVIEW REQUIRED: an additive contract amendment of `src/chem/contracts.ts` in Part 5; no schema, DB_STORES or invariant change).
- The depiction path: the navigator asks `services.depictions.depict(structure, { width, height, showAtomMaps: false })` (`src/app/window/navigator-port.ts:21-22`; sizes from `STRUCTURE_AREA`); `DepictionOptions` = `width`, `height`, `showAtomMaps`, `highlightAtomMaps?` (`src/chem/contracts.ts:57-62`), validated by `depictionDetails` (`src/chem/depiction-options.ts:21-31`, 16..4096 px); `drawMol` (`src/chem/rdkit/draw.ts:32-50`) calls `mol.get_svg_with_highlights(JSON.stringify({ width, height[, atoms] }))`. The request key is `depictionKeyOf` = `hashParts(['depiction', format, value, width, height, showAtomMaps, highlightAtomMaps])` (`src/app/services/depiction.ts:51-54`); the worker's own cache key adds the toolkit name and version (`src/chem/cached-toolkit.ts:69`, 500 entries). So today NEITHER key has a mode: Part 4 must add it to BOTH.
- The SVG sanitiser's allowlist (`src/chem/svg/whitelist.ts:9-68`): elements svg, g, path, rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon, text, tspan (text kept only in text/tspan); presentation properties fill, stroke, stroke-width, -linecap, -linejoin, -miterlimit, -opacity, fill-opacity, opacity, fill-rule, stroke-dasharray, font-family, -size, -weight, -style, text-anchor, dominant-baseline; geometry width, height, viewBox, x, y, dx, dy, x1..y2, cx, cy, r, rx, ry, d, points, transform, class. `sanitizeSvg` is called on every drawing in the adapter (`src/chem/rdkit/adapter.ts:162`).
(c) The spike, against the real `@rdkit/rdkit` 2026.03.6 in Node (the MinimalLib the app ships)
(1) FIXED SCALE: PROVED, with one caveat. `fixedBondLength` is ignored when `width` and `height` are -1 (identical output for 30, 100 and 200) and gives bond = 1.5 x value only on an explicit canvas, where the drawing is scaled to FIT (not usable for equal bonds). What works is `{ width: -1, height: -1, scalingFactor: S }`: the canvas fits the molecule and the bond length is a constant times S. Measured bond lengths in SVG units (median of unlabelled bonds): S = 100: propane 146.05, C20 147.12, C8 146.63, cyclohexane 147.80, benzene 147.80, toluene 147.80; S = 400: 592.1 to 593.6. The spread (about 0.6% at S = 100, from RDKit rounding the canvas to whole numbers) is under 0.3 px at a display bond of 40 px, inside the "within 1 px" the equation needs. The UI therefore sets the displayed size = SVG size x (target bond / nominal bond), the nominal bond being a documented constant of the chem module (about 147.5 SVG units at S = 100), checked by a chem test. Snippet: `m.get_svg_with_highlights(JSON.stringify({ width: -1, height: -1, scalingFactor: 100 }))`.
(2) CONDENSED labels: PROVED. The drawing option `atomLabels` (atom index -> label) takes `<sub>` markup and draws the subscript; carbons in rings are left unlabelled so rings stay rings (benzene and cyclohexanol drawn unchanged). Snippet: `const j = JSON.parse(m.get_json()); const d = j.defaults.atom; const q = R.get_qmol('[R]'); const ringAtoms = new Set(JSON.parse(m.get_substruct_matches(q)).map(x => x.atoms[0]))` (a result with no match parses to `{}`: treat a non-array as none), then for each atom `i` with `(a.z ?? d.z) === 6` and not in `ringAtoms`: `h = a.impHs ?? d.impHs`; label `h === 0 ? 'C' : h === 1 ? 'CH' : 'CH<sub>' + h + '</sub>'`; draw with `{ width: -1, height: -1, scalingFactor: 100, atomLabels: labels }`. Seen (screenshot rendered in Chromium): ethanol CH3-CH2-OH, bromoethane CH3-CH2-Br, isobutene CH3-C(-CH3)=CH2, C20 all CH2 with CH3 ends, benzene a ring with no labels. The text is drawn as glyph `<path>` elements (no `<text>`).
(3) FULL: PROVED. `const molblock = m.add_hs(); const mh = R.get_mol(molblock); mh.get_svg_with_highlights(...)`: `add_hs()` returns a molblock WITH 2D coordinates for the new hydrogens; drawn from that, every H is its own labelled atom with a bond (ethanol 9 atoms and 6 H labels, benzene 12 and 6, C20 62 and 42). The stored structure is never touched (the molecule is a copy made for the drawing). Chains come out right-angled (a textbook's full structure) and a ring keeps its ring.
(4) SANITISER: the SVG of (2) and (3) passes the EXISTING sanitiser UNCHANGED, for all 18 drawings tried (6 structures x skeletal, condensed, full): `ok: true`, `elementsDropped 0`, `styleDeclarationsDropped 0`, `stylesRefused 0`, `textDropped 0`, and the same 6 attributes dropped as for a skeletal drawing today (the `xmlns:*` / `xml:space` family). No sanitiser change is needed.
Counts from the chem worker: `heavyAtomCount` exists; ring count is available from RDKit two ways, `JSON.parse(mol.get_descriptors()).NumRings` (benzylcyclohexanol: 2) and the SMARTS count `[R]@[R]` (ring bonds; used to prove "a ring stays a ring": cyclohexanol and benzene 6 ring bonds in every mode).
Conclusion: none of the STOP conditions holds ((1), (2), (3) done; (4) needs no sanitiser change; both counts can be had, ring count by an additive fact). Going on to Part 4.
Design notes for Parts 4 and 5 found while reading (not decisions): (i) `EquationTerm` has no record reference, so Part 5 adds `ref` (the species, class or reagent behind the term) to it: an additive field of a core/graph value, no schema change; (ii) the representation rule needs facts (heavy atoms, rings, formula) and a drawing per term, so the equation view needs a port to the chem service's facts (the family and inspector ports carry only depictions today); (iii) the card's phone and desktop equation are the same component today.
Changed existing tests (a flake of part 1, found by this part's check run): `editor-window.test.tsx` opened the palette without preloading its lazy chunk and raced it (2 tests failed once, passed on a rerun alone); it and four other window tests that open the palette (`export-entry`, `phone-home-window`, `phone-window`, `window`) now preload it once with `prefetchPalette()` in `beforeAll`, as the two files of part 1 already did. No behaviour changed.
`editor-window.test.tsx` also preloads the editor's lazy chunk (`@/features/workbench/layer`) once: its findBy lookups of the editor dialog timed out once on this slow machine (1 s default, the chunk's first load); no timeout was changed.

### Equation step, part 4 - the "Structures" setting (2026-10-17)

(a) The setting: `PanelValues.structureMode` (`'skeletal' | 'condensed' | 'full'`, default skeletal) in the `panels` uiState entry (`src/ui/state/panels.ts`): a tolerant parse (a bad value is reset to skeletal and reported in `resetFields`, the rest of the entry is kept), `setStructureMode`, and the value is written only when it is not the default (an entry that never chose a mode stays as it was; unknown fields are still kept). No schema or DB_STORES change: `uiState` is a free-form tolerant store.
(b) The chem worker makes the drawing from the mode: `DepictionOptions.mode?` (additive; `STRUCTURE_MODES` / `StructureMode` in `src/chem/contracts.ts`, which the presentation layers may import at run time), validated by `depictionDetails` (default skeletal, a bad mode is a `RangeError`). `src/chem/rdkit/modes.ts`: Condensed adds the drawing option `atomLabels` (every carbon that is not in a ring is labelled CH3 / CH2 / CH / C, the digit a `<sub>`; a charged, radical or isotope-labelled carbon keeps RDKit's own label); Full draws a COPY of the molecule from the molblock `add_hs()` writes (every hydrogen its own atom with its own bond); rings always stay rings (ring atoms come from SMARTS `[R]`). The stored structure is never touched (INV-11; a test parses it again after a Full drawing). Both depiction keys include the mode: `depictionKeyOf` (`src/app/services/depiction.ts`) and the worker's cache key (`src/chem/cached-toolkit.ts`), and the adapter's key hashes `details`, which now has `mode`; so three modes are three cache entries and a switch never shows the other mode's drawing. `RdkitMol` gained two OPTIONAL methods (`get_substruct_matches`, `add_hs`), so the fake RDKit module is unchanged (a mode drawn through it answers `unavailable` in words).
(c) The wiring: the depiction port gained `mode?()` and `onMode?(listener)` and a `mode` argument on `keyOf` / `depict` (`DepictionPort` in `src/render/svg`, `NavigatorDepictions`). The binding reads the mode when it makes a key and KEEPS it with the structure, so a fetch draws in the mode of ITS key even if the setting changed in between. Who asks again after a change: the family page (its env is made again), the inspector's structure (`useStructureMode`), and the map (the pipeline rebuilds its scene on `onMode`, reusing the layout: the same request). The app's port (`createNavigatorPorts`, a fifth argument `structures`, from the panels store in `main.tsx`) fires `onMode` only when the mode itself changes, not for a drag of the inspector.
(c2) Where: a "Structures" `SegmentedControl` (new primitive: native radio buttons in one group, so one tab stop and the browser's arrow keys, a status line "Structures: Condensed" for a screen reader, 44 px segments, the chosen one also underlined) in the family page's TOOLBAR (desktop and phone; it stays in view while the list scrolls: in the header item it scrolled away with the list, which the e2e run showed), in More on the phone (a "Structures" section), and three palette commands ("Structures: Skeletal / Condensed / Full", the chosen one unavailable with "it is already chosen"; the keywords of 'full' include "show all atoms").
(d) Tests first, then the code: `tests/integration/chem-modes.test.ts` (real RDKit: three different drawings of CCO, CCBr, isobutene and ethylbenzene, the default equals skeletal, Condensed 3 labels against 1 for ethanol, Full 7 labels and 8 bonds, benzene and cyclohexanol keep their 6 ring bonds in every mode, only the side chain of toluene is labelled, a mapped structure in every mode, INV-11); `cache.test.ts` (the mode is in the cache key, a stub toolkit); `depiction.test.ts` (three keys); `panels.test.ts` (+3); `segmented-control.test.tsx` (5); `depictions.test.ts` (+4: a key per mode, the fetch draws in its key's mode, `useStructureMode`); `navigator-port.test.ts` (+3); `pipeline.test.ts` (+1); `navigator-family.test.tsx` (+2: the control, a saved Full); `palette-window.test.tsx` (+2); `phone-window.test.tsx` (+1); `depiction-mode.test.tsx` (the inspector); e2e `tests/e2e/structures.spec.ts` in the three engines (switch to Condensed: the PCC card's ethanol picture changes (more dark pixels: the labels), comes back after a reload, and returns to the first picture on Skeletal; the palette's "Structures: Full"; 0 securitypolicyviolation events; axe 29 rules, 0 problems).
Changed existing tests, with the reason: `src/chem/cache.test.ts` (the pinned `depictionDetails` result and key order gain `mode`), `src/ui/state/panels.test.ts` (two `toEqual` of the parsed values gain `structureMode: 'skeletal'`; the saved objects are unchanged because the default is not written). `test-support/navigator-kit.ts` (`fakeDepictions` keys carry `#<mode>` for a mode other than skeletal, so every skeletal key is what it was) and `window-kit.tsx` (`fakeApp` gives the navigator ports the Structures setting from its panels store) are helpers.

### Step 6.1b, part 1 - palette wait and long names (2026-10-18)

**The editor.spec flake: cause found, in the product.** Reproduced in Chromium (3 failures in 8 runs). The failure page showed the Search dialog open, the chunk loaded, the query answered: `No results for "renamed".` The lazy palette (prefetch, chunk cache, a query before the chunk is ready) is NOT involved: the answer was a real answer of the search worker. The index had not followed the Save yet: the search sync sends a commit's documents after `SEARCH_QUIET_MS` (200 ms) and the spec opened the palette and typed inside that window (it comes right after a family-page double click). The palette answered once, from the index as it was, said "No results" and never asked again, so the spec's 60 s wait for the option waited on a list that could not change. A query could be answered from a stale index without saying so. Why it began after 3c39e9c: the lazy chunk and the idle prefetch moved work around the window; the window itself is old.
**Fix (product).** `SearchPorts.indexState()` (optional): `current` / `catching_up` / `failed`, made in `src/app/window/search-port.ts` (`indexStateOf`) from the search sync's status and the store revision. The palette model never takes an answer from an index that is `catching_up` as final: it says "Search is catching up with your latest change", asks again every 500 ms (the NOT_READY bound, 20 asks), then shows the answer with "The results may not include your latest change." (logged `search_index_behind`). A `failed` sync is said in words next to the answer. The spec's `searchFor` helper waits for neither "starting" nor "catching up" (a real condition; no sleep, no timeout change, no assertion weakened). Proof: `--repeat-each=20` Chromium 20 of 20 (3 of 8 failed before); Firefox and WebKit once each, passed.
**Long names.** New `tests/e2e/equation-long-name.spec.ts`: Ethanol renamed to a 60-character name through the Edit names editor (the test's own data), the PCC card's full equation opened at 1280x800, Pixel 7 and iPhone 14; every name and word measured against every other box of the card (drawings, pluses, arrow, links, text) and the card's bottom edge. Result: NO overlap in any of the three; the name wraps to 3 lines in the 128 px desktop column and 2 on the phone, the estimate reserves 3 lines, and the card's own padding absorbs the rest. The `--hang` estimate is therefore kept (no change to `hang.ts`). The measurement itself is proven able to fail (a paragraph placed over a name is reported). Component test: `hang.test.ts` (60 characters reserve 3 lines + gap, never less than a shorter name). Screenshots: screenshots/equation-long-name-1280x800.png, screenshots/phone-equation-long-name-pixel7.png (iPhone: -iphone14.png).
Changed existing tests: none changed; `palette-model.test.ts` rig gained the optional `indexState` port (+3 tests).

### Step 6.1b, part 2 - the follower's search sync follows remote edits (2026-10-18)

How the sync tells the two apart: it could not from the ChangeSet as it was (both are `cause: 'remote'`, only the label differs); the smallest additive marker is `ChangeSet.reloaded?: true` (Amendments, REVIEW REQUIRED). `applyRemote`'s ChangeSet is analysed like a commit (changed records and fan-out, `REFRESH_CAP`, backlog, unchanged documents not sent); a `reload`'s stays ONE full load; a revision mismatch in the worker still falls back to ONE full load (integration test). One more place had the same blanket rule: `DerivedIndexes` (the full indexes the search sync reads) dropped and rebuilt on every `remote` ChangeSet, which would have kept the cost at a full index build; it now applies a mirrored span incrementally (property test P-07 proves current() equals a build after every span and reload).
Tests: unit `fanout.test.ts` (+1, one changed), `sync-remote.test.ts` (4: one-document update, a coalesced span, a deletion, a reload = ONE full load, each equal to a fresh build), `derived-indexes.test.ts` (+1; "a remote span or reload" renamed "a reload"), integration `app-services-follower-search.test.ts` (writer rename reaches the follower's index with no second full load, new name found, old not; a worker revision mismatch = ONE full load), e2e `follower-search.spec.ts` in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (writer renames and saves; the follower's palette finds the new name and not the old; its Edit names is unavailable with its reason).
Benchmark (`tests/perf/follower-search.bench.ts`; speed check 0.60 s before it; main thread only, the worker's update is a stub; design tier; mean of 4,000 / 13 samples): after, incremental 0.75 ms (p99 1.3 ms); before, as a reload (indexes built again, one full load) 232-238 ms. About 310x.
Changed existing tests: `fanout.test.ts` "replace and remote changes ask for a full load" now says `replace` and `remote` + `reloaded` (an unmarked `remote` is analysed since this step); `tests/property/derived-indexes.test.ts` P-07 asserted "never applied one by one" after a span too, now only after a reload (a span is applied, and equals a build); `derived-indexes.test.ts` titles. New budget entries for the two new benches (budgetMs null; no existing budget changed). openItem 23 CLOSED.

### Step 6.1b, part 4 - periodic snapshots through the compute worker (2026-10-18)

In the WRITER tab only (a follower, a read-only tab and a session with nothing saved take none; a promoted follower starts when it becomes the writer), the existing policy (30 minutes of activity or 200 revisions, injected clock) decides; when due, the compute worker builds the bytes from its replica (`snapshotBuild('periodic')`, after the replica has caught up) and they are stored with `storeSnapshotBytes(reason 'periodic', revision)`. STALE_REVISION (the data moved on while the bytes were built, from the replica or the adapter): nothing is stored, the policy stays due, the next ChangeSet tries again (no timer, no loop). Pruning to the newest five periodic snapshots is `storeSnapshotBytes`'s own (same transaction; mandatory and manual snapshots are never pruned). Visible: the status line (so the desktop line and the phone More > Status dialog, which shows the same line) gains "Automatic snapshots: last at <UTC time> (N kept)" or "none yet"; a failure is a log event (`periodic_snapshot_failed`) and "last attempt failed: <reason>" (no banner); a stale attempt is only a log event.
Tests: `periodic-flow.test.ts` (5, fakes), integration `app-services-periodic.test.ts` (9; injected clock: 200 revisions -> one; 30 minutes -> one; an idle gap and one edit -> none; a 6th prunes the oldest; STALE_REVISION stores nothing and the next ChangeSet stores one; a failing build is words and clears on success; a follower and a session-only tab take none; a promoted follower starts; a periodic snapshot restores like any), `banners.test.ts` and `status-parts.test.tsx` (the words). Test-support: `TestEnv.advanceMs`.
Timing (speed check 0.61 s; `tests/perf/periodic-snapshot.bench.ts`, a real worker thread, fake-indexeddb, design tier dense, snapshot 417,913 bytes): the build is in the worker and no longer on the main thread (it was 395 ms there, the Gate C list); end to end wall clock 254-262 ms (not the main thread's time); main thread: store with pruning 0.48-0.51 ms (fake-indexeddb, which costs more than a real one), receiving the answer under 0.01 ms (the buffer is transferred). New budget entries only (budgetMs null). openItem 119 CLOSED.
Changed existing tests: `tests/integration/app-services.test.ts` lists the members of `AppServices`; `snapshotsIdle` is added to the list (a new service member). `AppStatus` gained a field with a default.

## Outcome groups step

### Outcome groups step, part 1 - fact sheet (2026-10-19)

No product code. Every line below was read in the files named (not guessed); the demo was read from `data/seed/demo.orn.json` (27 reactions: 21 with one outcome, 1 with none, 5 with two).

**How a card turns outcomes into rows (desktop AND phone: one component, `layout` only changes the drawing).**
- The study (`src/core/graph/family/study.ts:105-161`) takes the roll-up candidates of the hub. A candidate is ONE MAIN PRODUCT of one outcome (`src/core/indexes/navigator-rollup.ts:196-215`; coproducts and byproducts are not candidates). They are gathered per (family group, reaction) and then PER OUTCOME ID (`study.ts:114-116`, `144-161`). A card therefore holds only the outcomes whose main product resolves to the card's group; an outcome that lands in another group is counted in `card.elsewhere` ("Also gives → Alkenes (443 K)", `study.ts:162-165`, `family-card.tsx:130-141`).
- `family-card.tsx:126-128` renders ONE `OutcomeRow` per `FamilyCardOutcome`: `family-card.tsx:62-92`. Each row is a COMPLETE scheme of its own: the carried substrate (`card.substrate`, ONE reactant, the primary substrate; not every reactant), its own arrow (`Arrow`, desktop `family-card.tsx:49-60`; `DownArrow`, phone `30-47`), then the products. So two outcomes of one reaction draw the substrate and the arrow TWICE, one scheme under the other, with nothing between them (the user's complaint). One row = one outcome, not one variant.
- Products of a row: `outcome.products`, each `Structure` with `caption = selectivity word` (`family-card.tsx:81-86`, word from `selectivityWordOf`, `src/core/graph/selectivity-word.ts:166`; `unspecified` has none), joined by "+".

**Condition variants on the arrow.** Per outcome: `arrowTextOf(reaction, { conditionVariantIds: o.variantIds, ... })` (`study.ts:151-157`). A participant listed in some variant is on the arrow only under those variants (`arrow-text.ts:103-106`); the variant's condition fields are laid over the stage's ONLY when the outcome has exactly ONE variant (`arrow-text.ts:154-161`, `effectiveParameters`). An empty set shows only what is common to every variant.

**Where "Show full equation" is attached.** On the card: one per outcome, directly under that outcome's row (`family-card.tsx:89` -> `FullEquationView`, `family-equation.tsx:15-40`; the `equation` is `fullEquationOf(reaction, stored outcome)`, `study.ts:158-159`). In the inspector: ONE disclosure for the reaction with a list of one scheme per outcome, labelled with the outcome label when there are several (`src/features/inspector/equation.tsx:15-87`, used at `view-reaction.tsx:149`; `fullEquationsOfReaction`, `full-equation.ts:133-150`). The inspector's reaction view also lists outcomes as TEXT rows (`view-reaction.tsx:92-107`, L2 list; `109-135`, L3 detail with Selectivity, Isomer group, Regiochemistry, Condition variants), not as schemes.

**Byproducts per outcome.** `fullEquationOf` (`full-equation.ts:60-130`) writes ALL products of THAT outcome in stored order (`outcome.products.map`, line 91): each with its role word (`coproduct`/`byproduct`) except main products; the selectivity word is attached ONCE, to the LAST main product of the outcome, with "both"/"all" when it has several main products (`88-105`). Reactants: every reactant participant that applies to the outcome's variants (`72-87`). So today a byproduct shared by two outcomes (water) is written in each outcome's own equation; nothing is shared or de-duplicated.

**Do regiochemistry and isomerGroup reach the card?** NO. Neither is on `NavigatorCandidate` (`navigator-rollup.ts:196-208`), `Production` (`src/core/indexes/contracts.ts:41-47`), `FamilyProduct`/`FamilyCardOutcome` (`src/core/graph/family/types.ts:16-30`) or `FullEquation`. They are read only by the inspector's L3 detail (`view-reaction.tsx:114-115`), the search document (`src/search/document/parts.ts`) and validation (`src/core/validation/rules/reactions.ts`). The study already holds the stored outcome (`study.ts:158`), so the card can carry `regiochemistry` WITHOUT an index or schema change (Part 2). The field is free label text (`LabelTextSchema`, `src/core/schema/reaction.ts:161-163`), not an enum.

**Demo reactions with 2+ outcomes (all five; products main unless noted).**
- `rxn_r-2-bromobutane-alc-koh` (E2): `out_...-1` major, regio "Saytzeff", but-2-ene; `out_...-2` minor, regio "Hofmann", but-1-ene. conditionVariantIds: [] and [] (no variants in the reaction). Same set -> ONE group of 2. Both products are alkenes: one card, two rows today.
- `rxn_propene-hbr`: `-1` major "Markovnikov", 2-bromopropane; `-2` minor "anti-Markovnikov", 1-bromopropane; [] and [] -> ONE group of 2 (isomerGroup "HBr addition regioisomers" on both).
- `rxn_propene-hbr-peroxide`: `-1` major "anti-Markovnikov", `-2` minor "Markovnikov"; [] and [] -> ONE group of 2.
- `rxn_ethanol-conc-h2so4`: `-1` major, [cvr_ethanol-conc-h2so4-1 = "413 K, excess ethanol"], main diethyl ether + byproduct water; `-2` major, [cvr_...-2 = "443 K, excess acid"], main ethene + byproduct water. Disjoint sets -> TWO groups of 1. NOTE: on the family page diethyl ether (Ethers) and ethene (Alkenes) are in DIFFERENT families, so the study already puts them on two different cards joined by "Also gives → Alkenes (443 K)" (e2e `family.spec.ts:92-97`, `navigator-family.test.tsx:124-125`). A card with two bordered groups does NOT arise from this reaction on the family page; it arises only where the reader sees all outcomes of the reaction (the inspector's full equation) or in a card built by a test.
- `rxn_ethanal-aldol`: `-1` major [cvr_ethanal-aldol-1 = "Base-catalysed (dilute NaOH, cold)", catalyst NaOH], `-2` major [cvr_ethanal-aldol-2 = "Acid-catalysed", catalyst hydronium]; both main 3-hydroxybutanal. Disjoint sets, ONE family group (same product species) -> the real two-group CARD of the demo (2 bordered groups, one outcome each, different arrows).
Other regiochemistry in the demo: `rxn_r-2-bromobutane-aq-koh` has ONE outcome with "substitution". All regiochemistry words in the demo: Markovnikov, anti-Markovnikov, Saytzeff, Hofmann, substitution.

**Partly overlapping variant sets?** NONE. Every pair of outcomes in the demo is either equal (both empty) or disjoint (single, different variants). The STOP condition is not met. (Not covered by the demo or by the brief, and handled in Part 2 as the rule says: an outcome with an EMPTY set is a group of its own, apart from outcomes with named variants; REVIEW REQUIRED there.)

### Outcome groups step, part 2 - outcome groups in the card and the full equation (2026-10-19)

No schema, DB_STORES, CSP, `_headers` or sanitiser change; no index change (the study already holds the stored outcome, so `regiochemistry` reaches the card from there).
**Group rule** (`src/core/graph/outcome-groups.ts`, pure, tested): two outcomes are in one group exactly when their condition-variant SETS are equal (order and repeats ignored; the empty set is a set like another); groups in the order of their first outcome; inside a group exclusive, major, minor, trace, mixture component, unspecified (the schema's `SELECTIVITIES` order, an unknown value last), then stored order. `outcomeWordOf(selectivity, regiochemistry)`: "major · Saytzeff".
**Study** (`family/groups.ts`, `types.ts`, `study.ts`): `FamilyCard.groups: FamilyOutcomeGroup[]` replaces `FamilyCard.outcomes`; a group has `key`, `conditionVariantIds`, `heading`, `outcomes` (each with `selectivity`, `regiochemistry?`, `word`), ONE `arrowText` and ONE `equation`. `FamilyCardOutcome` lost `arrowText` and `equation` (they live on the group). Outcomes are ordered by the record's stored order before the rule runs (was: outcome ID).
**Equation** (`full-equation.ts`): `fullEquationOfGroup(reaction, outcomes, ctx)`; `fullEquationOf` is the group of one. Reactants and arrow once; main products of each outcome in group order, each outcome's word on its last main (`(both exclusive)` unchanged inside one outcome); then coproducts and byproducts, a species shared by outcomes written once by `RecordRef` (kind + ID), never by name or formula. Additive fields: `EquationTerm.regiochemistry`, `FullEquation.outcomeIds`. `text` is the old one-line equation for ONE outcome and ONE sentence for a group of several ("(R)-2-bromobutane with alc. KOH, heat, basic medium gives But-2-ene (major) and But-1-ene (minor)"). `fullEquationsOfReaction` (the inspector) returns one equation per group.
**Card** (`family-card.tsx`): one scheme per group: the substrate and ONE arrow, then a product tile for each main product of each outcome (desktop: a column right of the arrow, major on top; phone: tiles side by side in a row that wraps under the down arrow; CSS `display: contents`), the word under each. One "Show full equation" per group. A card with 2+ groups: each group in a bordered `section` (aria-label and `h5` = heading); one group: no header. The open full equation is a panel (`details[data-equation-panel]`: 1 px `--color-rule` border, `--color-surface` tone; the card and the inspector). The Names switch moved inside the panel's padding.
**Demo findings (REVIEW REQUIRED, see part 1):** E2, propene + HBr, propene + HBr (peroxide): ONE group of two. Aldol: TWO groups (the real two-block card; its reaction has no stage, so its arrow states no condition and the heading is the variant's own label). EtOH + conc. H2SO4: ether (Ethers) and ethene (Alkenes) are different families, so on the family page they are two cards of one outcome each, joined by "Also gives"; the two-bordered-groups card with "At 413 K" / "At 443 K" is proved by a component test with the demo reaction's second product moved into the ether's family, and the inspector's equation shows both groups.
**Words shown from the demo (regiochemistry as stored):** Saytzeff, Hofmann (E2); Markovnikov, anti-Markovnikov (HBr, with and without peroxide). "substitution" (aq. KOH, ONE outcome) is not shown: a group of one outcome shows the selectivity word alone.
**Tests (first):** unit `outcome-groups.test.ts` (11: same set, empty set, order and repeats, disjoint, partial overlap, schema order, unknown last, words with and without regiochemistry), `family/groups.test.ts` (13: the demo E2, propene, aldol; "At 413 K"; empty set apart; shared byproduct once by ID; same name another ID twice; "(both exclusive)" inside an outcome; one outcome; regiochemistry alone; `headingOf`); component `family-card-groups.test.tsx` (10: E2 desktop and phone: reactant once, one arrow, two tiles, words, one "Show full equation", panel, sentence; two bordered groups with headers on both layouts; the aldol card; a one-outcome card unchanged); e2e `outcome-groups.spec.ts` (desktop: E2, aldol, ethanol card) and `phone-outcome-groups.spec.ts` (Pixel 7 Chromium, iPhone 14 WebKit; no sideways scroll, 0 CSP violations, axe). Chromium run of the new specs passed (the ethanol assertion was first too narrow: the first card of the pair can be the Alkenes one; fixed in the spec).
**Changed existing tests (one row per outcome became one scheme per group; `card.outcomes` became `card.groups`):** `study.test.ts` (3 expectations read `groups`), `full-equation.test.ts` (the per-card word check reads the group's equation), `family-equation.test.tsx` (the equation and arrow text are on the group), `family-items.test.ts` and `family-items.ts` (height guess counts outcomes over groups), `tests/property/family-study.test.ts` (outcome IDs read through groups), `equation-scheme.test.tsx` and `hang.test.ts` (the test helpers gained the new fields `regiochemistry` / `outcomeIds`).
Screenshots: screenshots/outcomes-e2-1280x800.png, outcomes-e2-equation-1280x800.png, outcomes-ethanol-h2so4-1280x800.png (the Ethers/Alkenes card; the real two-block card is outcomes-aldol-1280x800.png), phone-outcomes-e2-pixel7.png, phone-outcomes-e2-iphone14.png, phone-outcomes-e2-equation-pixel7.png.

### Step 6.2a, part 1 - fact sheet (2026-10-19)

Speed check 1.303 / 1.303 / 1.308 s (median 1.303 s: 0.003 s over the 1.3 s line; Part A and this part measure no timing, so the session goes on; it is checked again before Part 2's benchmark). No product code. Part A (the outcome groups review) is commit 983aaa0.

**a. Species schema** (`src/core/schema/substances.ts:72-93`, strictObject; primitives in `src/core/schema/primitives.ts`). Limits are `LIMITS` (primitives.ts:10-43). "Section" is the D2 section.
- `id` SpeciesId, required (generated from CommandContext), not shown. `kind` literal 'species', required, not shown.
- `names` required (primitives.ts:138): `canonical` NameText required (single line, not blank, max 300, no control/bidi chars); `display`, `iupac` NameText optional; `common[]`, `aliases[]` NameText, required arrays, max 64 each; `qualifier` LabelText (max 200) optional. Section: Names (the existing NamesSection).
- `speciesKind` required enum: molecule, ion, salt, radical, reactive_intermediate, element, polymer, unspecified (substances.ts:14-23; 'unspecified' is the empty value). Section: Identity.
- `structure` optional `{format: smiles|cxsmiles|molfile, value}`; value 1..1,000,000 chars, and 20,000 for the two line notations (primitives.ts:197-205). Section: Structure.
- `formula` LabelText optional (max 200, single line); `charge` integer -20..20 optional. Section: Formula and charge.
- `isotopeNote` ShortText optional (max 2,000). Section: Identity (the only other identity field the schema has).
- `classIds[]` ClassId, required array, max 256. Section: Classes.
- `stereo` optional `{kind: achiral|single_stereoisomer|racemic|meso|diastereomeric_mixture|unspecified, descriptors[] LabelText max 32 (required inside), note? RichText}`. Section: Stereo.
- `aromaticity` optional enum aromatic|antiaromatic|non_aromatic|unspecified. Section: Aromaticity claim.
- `properties[]` (max 64; each key enum, label?, value ShortText, note?, citations[]), `acidBaseNotes`, `studyNotes`, `notes` (RichText max 50,000, optional), `tags[]` (max 64, required), `citations[]` (max 64, required). Section: NONE in 6.2a: read-only with "Editing arrives in step 6.6", kept unchanged.
- `provenance` required `{origin, createdAt, updatedAt, importBatchId?, legacy?}`; `review` required `{lifecycle draft|published, status unreviewed|review_required|verified, confidence?, reasons[] (max 32), reviewedAt?}` (primitives.ts:165-190). Section: Review (lifecycle editable; status read-only). Provenance is not shown.
- A NEW species: every required field has a sensible empty value (names {canonical, common: [], aliases: []}, speciesKind 'unspecified', classIds [], properties [], tags [], citations [], provenance {origin 'user', createdAt = updatedAt = ctx time}, review {lifecycle 'draft', status 'unreviewed', reasons []}). The stop condition (no empty value) is NOT met. The empty canonical name does not pass L1 (NameText is not blank): Save is refused until a name is typed, which is right.

**b. Chem worker API** (`src/chem/contracts.ts`, `src/workers/chem/{client,handlers,specs,wire}.ts`). The main thread uses `ChemService` (client.ts:26-35): `parse(structure)` -> `ParseOutcome` (contracts.ts:56-59: `{ok:true, facts}`, or `{ok:false, reason:'invalid', problem:'unreadable'|'sanitisation', error}`, or reason `unavailable`|`timeout`). `StructureFacts` (contracts.ts:23-46): canonicalSmiles, formula (Hill), charge, heavyAtomCount, carbonCount, specified/unspecifiedStereocentres, hasDoubleBondStereo, cipCounts {R,S,r,s,E,Z}, aromatic, atomMaps, warnings. `depict(structure, {width,height,showAtomMaps,mode?,fixedScale?})` -> sanitised SVG `Depiction{key,svg,width,height}` or a failure value (`refused` when the sanitiser refuses); the Structures mode is `mode: skeletal|condensed|full` (contracts.ts:72-78, part of the depiction key). Also `checkSpecies`, `checkReaction`, `checkMechanism`, `matches(probes)`. Each call has a 2 s limit, is idempotent, retried once after a crash (specs.ts:11-19); a timeout restarts the worker. Errors are values (client.ts:37-47): `invalid` is the ONLY reason that says the structure is bad.
Limits are in the adapter (`src/chem/rdkit/adapter.ts:32-34`): 20,000 characters for smiles/cxsmiles, 1,000,000 for a molfile, and a molfile must contain "M  END" (`inputProblem`, exported from `@/chem`). Over the limit is refused before RDKit sees it (an `invalid`/`unreadable` value with the limit in words), never truncated. The UI checks the same limits itself, from `LIMITS` and `inputProblem` (no chemistry).

**c. How the CHEM rules are computed today.**
- CHEM-001/002 (`src/chem/checks/species.ts:34-48`): `checkOneSpecies` parses; `invalid`+`unreadable` -> CHEM-001 "The structure cannot be read: <error>."; `invalid`+`sanitisation` -> CHEM-002; `unavailable`/`timeout` -> `not_checked`, never a CHEM-001.
- CHEM-003 (species.ts:12-33): entered formula vs derived, by element COUNTS (`parseFormula`, `countDifferences`, formula.ts), never strings; a mismatch is a warning at path `formula`. CHEM-004 is the same for the charge.
- CHEM-007 (`plan-species.ts:54-108`): `membershipPlan(state, species)` builds one probe per class with `generic.smarts` (first 100, `MAX_CLASS_PROBES`); `ChemService.matches(probes)` answers per probe; `readMembership(state, species, plan, outcomes)` yields the drafts ("suggest_add" with `data.classId` when the class is not stated; ancestors count as stated). Both functions are PURE over a Species value and the state, so a DRAFT works with NO contract change (build a Species from the draft, plan, one `matches` call, read). "Classes whose SMARTS match this structure" therefore exists as plan + `matches`.
- CHEM-009 (`duplicates.ts`, `src/workers/chem/l4/groups.ts`): a DERIVED in-memory map canonical SMILES <-> species ids on the main-thread L4 service (`context.ts:87`), filled from `checkSpecies` results (`SpeciesCheckResult.canonicalSmiles`). `Groups.membersOf(canonical)` is exactly "species by canonical structure", but the `L4Service` interface (l4/contracts.ts:67-92) does NOT expose it. A draft needs `chem.checkSpecies([request])` for its canonical SMILES (exists) plus ONE additive L4Service method `speciesWithCanonical(canonical)` reading `groups.membersOf`. RDKit's canonical SMILES keeps atom maps (a mapped structure and its unmapped twin differ); the duplicate check uses the same comparison.
Result: CHEM-007 needs no contract change; CHEM-009 needs ONE additive method on the main-side L4 service (not a worker method). The stop condition is NOT met.

**d. SPC-001** (`src/core/validation/rules/substances.ts:70-90`, helpers :15-33): L3 warning. `twinsOf`: `ctx.indexes.byFoldedName('species', fold(names.canonical))` minus the record itself, kept when the folded canonical names are equal AND the folded QUALIFIERS are equal (a different qualifier tells them apart). Peers (`namePeers`): every folded name of the record (`foldedNamesOf`, `src/core/indexes/names.ts:13`: canonical, display, iupac, common, aliases; the qualifier is not a name). The folding function is `fold` in `src/core/text/normalizer.ts:70` (NFKC, lower case, ß, NFD without combining marks, Greek letters spelled out, apostrophes removed, dashes -> spaces except a charge sign, whitespace collapsed, trimmed).

**e. Dry run in the compute worker.** The replica (`src/workers/compute/replica.ts`) holds {state, revision, indexes, findings}. Its `apply` updates the indexes IN PLACE (`indexEngine.apply` "consumes the old handle", replica.ts:152, :164), so a dry `apply` is NOT an option. `prepare` (replica.ts:96-127) rebuilds ALL indexes for a whole state: far too slow for a live check, and it would replace the pending import state. BUT the validator is pure: `validateTouchedByRule(state, indexes, touched, previous, known)` (validator.ts:114-146) only reads its arguments (`commitTouched` is what writes, into a store the caller passes), and a rule's context is only `{state, indexes}`, read through `get`, `byFoldedName`, `referrersOf`, `definersOf`, `linkersOf`, `ancestorsOf`, `descendantsOf` (grep of `ctx.indexes.` in `rules/`). So a dry run is possible WITHOUT cloning or mutating the replica's indexes: (1) a state overlay `{...state, records: {...records, species: {...table, [id]: draft}}}` (one shallow copy of one table, O(species); the replica's frozen state is untouched); (2) a READ-ONLY index view delegating every method to the replica's indexes except `get(draftId)` (the draft) and `byFoldedName` (the draft's own names instead of the stored ones); (3) a pure single-record check running `parseRecord` (L1), then the L2 and L3 rules of the draft's kind, as `findingsOf` does (validator.ts:36-41, not exported). Cost: the table copy plus the rules of ONE record; measured in Part 2. The only addition is exporting a single-record check from `src/core/validation` (additive function; no schema or DB change). Said now: the dry run answers the DRAFT's own findings (L1-L3 of that record, SPC-001 against the replica's names); findings it would CAUSE on other records are not in scope (D2: "findings for the draft's fields").
Stop conditions of Part 1: NOT met (no clone, no mutation; CHEM-007 and CHEM-009 need no worker method). Going on.
REVIEW REQUIRED: the Part 2 dry run is an overlay (a table copy plus a delegating read-only index view), not the replica's apply and not a clone; and two additive exports: a single-record L1-L3 function in core/validation, and `speciesWithCanonical` on the L4 service. Say if you prefer otherwise.
