**c. HIER cycles.** HIER-001 (rules/substances.ts:293-321, L3 ERROR, global): for each parent `p` of a class, cyclic when `p === id` or `ancestorsOf('class', p)` contains `id`; at path `parentIds[i]`. The walks are the cycle-safe breadth-first `closure` (core/indexes/hierarchy.ts:32-45), exposed as `ancestorsOf` / `descendantsOf` on the indexes (core/indexes/contracts.ts:74-76). It runs at Save in the store's gate (and in the 6.2a dry run). A picker CAN ask before saving: `p` makes a cycle for class `c` exactly when `p === c` or `p` is in `descendantsOf('class', c)` (p's ancestors contain c iff p is below c). The class picker port already has `indexes()` (app/window/class-picker-port.ts:21). A NEW class has no descendants, so nothing is refused except itself. Reason words: "is this class" / "is below this class".
HIER-003 (rules/substances.ts:346-370, L3 ERROR): `reagentCycle` (:54-69) walks the REAGENT-kind components (`ref.kind === 'reagent'`) from the record, bounded by `MAX_WALK_NODES` = 10,000 (helpers.ts:48). Species and class components cannot make a cycle; only reagent components can. A picker asks: candidate reagent `r` makes a cycle for reagent `g` when `r === g` or `g` is reached by walking down `r`'s reagent components (equivalently `r` is in the upstream closure of `g` through `referrersOf` with owner kind reagent and path under `components`, the rule's own `peers`, :352-360).

**d. Chem worker.** (a) VALIDATE A SMARTS: YES today, no change. `ChemService.matches(probes)` (workers/chem/client.ts:31) runs `toolkit.matchesSmarts(structure, smarts)` (chem/checks/run.ts:55-58; adapter.ts:174-203); an unreadable pattern is `{ok:false, reason:'invalid_smarts', error}` (contracts.ts:106-109). A one-probe call with a fixed one-atom structure ('C') validates a SMARTS alone. Proved with real RDKit (scratch test, removed): an unclosed bracket pattern -> invalid_smarts "RDKit cannot read this SMARTS"; "[CX4][OX2H]" -> ok. Limits: 1 to 20,000 characters. (b) DRAW AN R-LABELLED CXSMILES: YES today, no change. Real RDKit, `[*]C(O)CO |$R;;;;$|`: `parse` is ok, canonicalSmiles "*C(O)CO", formula undefined with the warning "formula: an atom is a dummy or not an element in the table" (so no formula is derived, as D1 wants), and `depict` is ok (a sanitised SVG that differs from the same SMILES without labels: the label is drawn). The structure panel's `port.parse` / `depictions` take any StructureRep; the generic mode only has to hide the facts table and "Use derived formula". No chem-worker method is added.
Stop conditions of Part 1: NOT met (classKind handled as above; the SMARTS check and the generic drawing need zero new methods). Going on.

**e. Other facts the parts use.** A profile needs an ID inside a pure recipe: the editor port gets an additive `newId(prefix)` (from the CommandContext). The existing class picker (`ClassPickerPort`) becomes the generic `RecordPickerPort` (kinds species, class, reagent) of D4. Components accept species, class AND reagent refs (the schema's SubstanceRef): without reagent refs there is no cycle to refuse, so HIER-003 would be unreachable. The blank draft of 6.2a is extended for 'class' and 'reagent' (core/editing/blank.ts).

**a. Reaction schema, top level** (`src/core/schema/reaction.ts:211-254`, strictObject; limits `LIMITS`, primitives.ts:10-37: name 300, label 200, shortText 2,000, richText 50,000, aliases 64, participants 64, stages 16, outcomes 32). "Section" is the D1 section.

- `name` NameText required (non-blank, max 300, single line; :214): Identity. **A reaction has `name` + `aliases`, NOT `Names`** (no canonical / common / qualifier): the shared `NamesSection` (which edits `names`) cannot be used as is; D1 says "through NamesSection if the schema has Names" and the schema does not (REVIEW REQUIRED 1).
- `aliases[]` NameText, required, max 64 (:215): Identity.
- `scope` enum generic | specific, required (:217): Identity. **No empty value.**
- `instanceOfId` ReactionId optional (:219; RXN-013 at reactions-more.ts:23-60: target generic, this one specific, no chains): Identity (picker of GENERIC reactions).
- `purposes[]` enum REACTION_PURPOSES (7 values, :201-209), required, max 7: Identity ("the other identity fields the schema has").
- `namedReactionIds[]` (max 16), `transformationIds[]` (16), `reactionTypes[]` and `mechanismClasses[]` ({conceptId, certainty}, 16), `conceptIds[]`, `prerequisiteConceptIds[]` (256), `mechanismIds[]` (16): required arrays; read-only ("Editing arrives in step 6.5 / 6.6"), kept unchanged.
- `participants[]` required, max 64 (:227): Participants. `stages[]` required, max 16 (:228): Stages.
- `conditionVariants[]` (max 16), `outcomes[]` (32), `intermediates[]` (32): required arrays; read-only summaries ("step 6.4" for conditions, variants and outcomes; mechanism links 6.5), kept unchanged.
- `reversibility` {kind enum equilibrium | reversible_under_other_conditions | irreversible | unknown, note?} required (:233): read-only summary (classification, "step 6.5"); its empty value is `unknown`.
- `selectivityNotes?`, `generalizedEquation?` (ShortText), `mappedReaction?`, `limitations?`, `difficulty?`, `studyNotes?`, `notes?`: optional, read-only, kept. `tags[]`, `citations[]` required, `provenance`, `review` required (recordMetaShape, primitives.ts:209-214): Review (lifecycle editable, status read-only, as for species); tags and citations read-only.
- The legacy `reagentFamily` has no field: it is kept in `provenance.legacy.unmapped.reagentFamily` (classify-fields.ts:217-224, classify-map.test.ts:136), so D6's read-only line reads that path.

**b. Participant** (reaction.ts:68-84) and its limits: `id` ParticipantId (`prt`, ids.ts:104) required, from the session's `newId`; `ref` SubstanceRef species | class | reagent (refs.ts:10-14) required; `role` enum required; `coefficient?` PositiveNumber (finite, > 0); `phase?` enum; `strength?` enum; `dry?` boolean; `quantity?` {equivalents? PositiveNumber, qualifier? enum, text? LabelText}; `profileId?` ReagentProfileId, only when `ref.kind === 'reagent'` and a profile of THAT reagent (RXN-011 reactions.ts:211, REF-005, references.ts:137-142); `flags?` {contributesAtoms?, consumed?, catalytic?} booleans; `isPrimarySubstrate?`; `originalText?` ShortText (read-only line); `note?` RichText (not in D2: read-only, kept).
- Roles (reaction.ts:38-48): reactant, reagent, catalyst, solvent, initiator, promoter, additive, workup_reagent, spectator. Defaults (DOMAIN_MODEL §6.2), contributesAtoms / consumed / catalytic: reactant yes/yes/no; reagent yes/yes/no; catalyst no/no/yes; solvent no/no/no; initiator no/yes/no; promoter no/no/no; additive no/no/no; workup_reagent yes/yes/no; spectator never/no/no. Overrides: RXN-004 (spectator + contributesAtoms, ERROR, reactions.ts:65), RXN-005 (catalyst + consumed, WARNING, :84).
- Phases (:51): s, l, g, aq, alc, soln, melt. Strengths (:52): dilute, concentrated, fuming, glacial, saturated. Quantity qualifiers (:53): catalytic, excess, limiting, stoichiometric, trace.
- Section: Participants (D2) for everything except `note`.

**c. Stage** (reaction.ts:90-98): `id` StageId (`stg`, ids.ts:105) required; `kind` enum reaction | workup | quench | activation | purification (:87) required; `label?` LabelText; `participantIds[]` ParticipantId, required, max 64; `parameters` ConditionParameters required (the required arrays are solventCharacter, activation, other, parsedFields, conditions.ts:76-92); `originalText?` ShortText. Section: Stages (D3) for kind, label and the order; `parameters` and `originalText` read-only until 6.4, kept.
- **How a participant refers to a stage: it does not.** `Participant` has no `stage` field; the stage lists its participants (`stages[].participantIds[]`, a `local` reference to `participants`, delete policy detach: references.ts:143). A participant's stage is DERIVED: the stage whose `participantIds` has its ID (`stagesOfParticipants`, reaction-utils.ts:16-24). RXN-007 (reactions.ts:118-135, ERROR): with stages present every participant is in exactly one. So the D2 "stage" picker is a derived choice that moves the ID between two stages' lists (one recipe, one undo step). Other references to a stage: `conditionVariants[].stageId` and `intermediates[].stageId` (references.ts:144, :173, detach); both are read-only in 6.3a, so removing a stage they name must be REFUSED in words (not detached silently): proposed for Part 4.
- Stage order is array order (reaction.ts:89).

**d. A NEW reaction** (every required field and its empty value; `blankDraft` has none for reactions today, core/editing/blank.ts:19-33): `name` '' (L1 refuses Save, like the empty canonical name); `aliases` []; **`scope` ABSENT** ("Choose a scope", L1 refuses Save with the schema's words until chosen: the pattern the reviewer approved for `classKind` in 6.2b; no default is invented); `purposes` []; `namedReactionIds`, `transformationIds`, `reactionTypes`, `mechanismClasses`, `conceptIds`, `prerequisiteConceptIds`, `mechanismIds` []; `participants` []; `stages` [] (**the schema does NOT need a stage**: RXN-007 is silent with none; so a new reaction starts with no stage, D4's "one empty stage if the schema needs one" does not apply; the first stage the user adds takes every existing participant, said in words, because "stages present" needs each participant in exactly one); `conditionVariants`, `outcomes`, `intermediates` []; `reversibility` {kind 'unknown'}; `tags` [], `citations` []; `provenance` {origin 'user', createdAt = updatedAt = ctx time}; `review` {draft, unreviewed, reasons []}. Result: Save is refused only for the name and the scope; with no outcomes it saves as a draft with RXN-002 (a WARNING for a draft; RXN-001 too when there is no reactant); Published is refused while RXN-002 is an ERROR for published (`lifecycleSeverity`).

**e. The reorder builder** (`core/commands/builders/reorder.ts:41-71`): a STORE command builder (`record.update` of the whole record). It needs distinct item IDs and `orderedIds` to be a permutation (every current ID exactly once, no extras, no repeats: :28-39, "The new order must list every current item exactly once."); a missing array or ID is VALIDATION_FAILED; `within` reaches the array of one nested item. It is not used by editor sessions (they edit a draft with Immer recipes, like `moveComponent` in reagent-model.ts); the reaction model's move recipes follow the same permutation rule and are tested against it. Reordering participants or stages changes no reference (stages hold participant IDs).

**f. Can the dry run validate a REACTION draft without cloning or mutating the replica? YES, with no change to the approach.** `dryRun` (workers/compute/dry-run.ts:42-52) is generic over the kind: the overlay copies ONE table shallowly (`{ ...table, [id]: draft }`; the record objects are shared, not cloned) and the index view delegates to the replica's indexes except `get` of the draft's ID and `byFoldedName`. Proved (scratch run on the real demo; the scripts are in the scratchpad, not committed): a draft of a demo reaction with a participant `spc_nope` gives `REF-001 error participants[3].ref`; a blank-like draft gives only the L1 SCHEMA findings (name, a malformed ID); the replica's reaction table is identical before and after (JSON equal) and the new ID is absent from the indexes. What the reaction rules read: `ctx.indexes.get(id)` (existence: REF-001..005, RXN-013's target via `existing`, helpers.ts:30-40); `indexes.referrersOf(reaction.id)` (RXN-018, reactions-more.ts:98); `indexes.definersOf(nestedId)` (REF-006, references.ts:99 and reference-analysis.ts:127, which excludes the record's own ID); `ctx.state.records[kind]` only in `allOfKinds` (peers of route rules, not reaction rules). All are delegated to the replica unchanged and the overlay answers `get` of the draft's own ID, so the only table that must hold the draft is `records.reaction` (the same one-table copy). No new table or index is needed: Part 2 adds tests (REF-001 on a dangling participant, the replica deep-equal) and the timing, not a new mechanism. Honest limit (as for species): findings a reaction draft would cause on OTHER records (relationships naming it, routes using it) are the store's gate's at Save.

**g. Demo reactions that would trigger D5's rule: NONE, and the rule already exists.** Scratch validation of the 27-reaction demo: reaction findings are RXN-016 info 16, RXN-002 warning 1, RVW-001 review_required 1; **RXN-021 fires on 0**. More important: **RXN-021 IS D5's rule.** VALIDATION_RULES row RXN-021 reads "Same substance twice with the same role (use a coefficient)", WARNING; it is built (reactions-more.ts:144-165): its key is substance | role | stage ids | condition-variant ids (`usageKey`, :13-19), so two uses in DIFFERENT stages or variants are silent (test reactions-more.test.ts:148-161: same stage -> warning at `participants[4].ref`, other stage -> nothing). D5 asks for "a new L3 rule (next free RXN number)... same substance, same role and same stage -> WARNING"; a new rule would raise a SECOND warning for the same condition. The open item "Consider a WARNING for the same substance listed twice in the same role and stage (use coefficient) - decide in Phase 6" was written without RXN-021 in mind; it stays open with a note. RXN-021's message today: "Participant N repeats participant M (same <kind>, same role). Use a coefficient instead." It does not name the role or the stage.

**STOP (the prompt: "anything here contradicts a doc"; "do not invent").** D5 contradicts the code and VALIDATION_RULES: its premise (no such rule) is false. Smallest proposed amendment, for the reviewer: do NOT add a rule; keep RXN-021 and (optionally) change its MESSAGE to "listed twice as <role> in stage <n>; use the coefficient instead" (one finding message and its test); the e2e (2) "the D5 warning appears when the same reactant is added twice in the same stage" then reads RXN-021 as it is. Parts 2 (the rule half), 3 and 4 are not started; the dry-run half of Part 2 and everything else is unaffected by this.

## Step 6.3b

### Step 6.3b, part 1 - fact sheet (2026-10-20)

Speed check 0.538 / 0.530 / 0.548 s (median 0.538 s). No product code; `tests/measure/reaction-preview.measure.ts` (informal, REPORTED, not in `npm test`) is the only file added besides this entry. Part A (6.3a review recorded) is commit 659eed8.

**Can the group builder and the full-equation builder take a draft reaction? YES, with no contract change and without writing the draft anywhere.**
- The CARD's own builder (`familyStudy`, `core/graph/family/study.ts:105-161`) cannot: it starts from the navigator roll-up INDEX (`rollup.candidatesFrom`, study.ts:104), and a draft is in no index. Its pieces can: `outcomeGroupsOf(reaction, entries, ctx)` (`family/groups.ts:39-73`) and the group rule `groupOutcomes` (`outcome-groups.ts:33`) take any outcomes, and `fullEquationOfGroup(reaction, outcomes, ctx)` (`full-equation.ts:91`) takes ANY `Reaction` value plus `{ schemes, describe, substanceOf, shownAsNode }`.
- The ready-made entry is `fullEquationsOfReaction(state, indexes, reaction)` (`full-equation.ts:187-203`), already used by the inspector (`features/inspector/equation.tsx:21`). It takes the reaction as an argument (never looks it up by ID), so a draft goes straight in. It groups with `groupOutcomes(reaction.outcomes)` (:196) and builds one `FullEquation` per group: the same groups, words ("major · Saytzeff") and arrow text the card's "Show full equation" shows.
- WHAT IT READS: the `CanonicalState` only through `createDescriber(state)` (`family/describe.ts:32-71`: species / reagent / class records by the participants' and products' refs, and a reagent's species); the indexes through `referrersOf(reaction.id)` (the draft's schemes, :190-195; none for a new reaction, then the role defaults apply) and `displayOf(ref)` (`showAsNode`, :201). It writes nothing; the draft is not in `state.records.reaction` and not in any index. No overlay is needed (the dry run needs one; this does not).
- WHAT CAN NOT be reused as is: (1) the card's scheme COMPONENT (`GroupScheme`, `features/navigator/family-card.tsx:69`) is a navigator feature file and draws ONE carried substrate, not every reactant; a workbench file cannot import it (no cross-feature imports). The shared component is `EquationScheme` (`render/equation/equation-scheme.tsx`), the very component behind the card's "Show full equation"; it draws all reactants, the arrow with the draft's reagents and conditions, and the products of the group. The preview uses it (REVIEW REQUIRED 1). (2) A reaction with NO outcome gives `groupOutcomes([])` = no equation, and `fullEquationOfGroup` throws on an empty list (:93). The "reactants and the arrow, no products yet" view needs ONE additive core function (the same arrow and reactant code, no outcome; `fullEquationOfGroup` unchanged).
- Where it runs: the main thread holds the state and indexes the inspector already reads (`env.state`, `ports.indexes.current()`), so the app fills one new OPTIONAL port field on `EditorPort` (`editor-contracts.ts`, additive, like `records?` and `structure?`) and the draw ports (`binding`, `facts`, the Structures names setting) the equation already uses. The answer is plain data (`FullEquation[]`).

**A participant with no substance.** The schema requires `ref`; the editor only adds a participant with a picked substance, but a recovered or hand-edited draft can lack it. The builders then THROW: `partOf` / `describe(ref)` read `ref.kind` (`describe.ts:33`; `arrow-text.ts:109-114`; `full-equation.ts:114`). A `ref` that points at a record that is gone does NOT throw: the ID is written (`describe` undefined, `nameOf` falls back to `ref.id`, `substanceOf` is `missing`). So the preview must check each participant first (a `ref` with a known kind and a non-empty ID) and say in words which one is missing, never calling the builder (D2); a dangling ref is drawn by its ID, as on a card.

**Cost** (`tests/measure/reaction-preview.measure.ts`, 300 samples after 30 warm-ups, hub_explosion state of 250 species; builder in the replica's own code, no thread): the largest design-tier reaction (`rxn_g-00000`: 2 participants, 0 stages, 1 outcome, 0 variants) mean 0.010 ms, p99 0.035 ms; the SCHEMA CEILING (64 participants, 16 stages, 32 outcomes in one group) mean 0.034 ms, p99 0.084 ms. The 400 ms debounce, not the build, sets the preview's latency; drawing is the depiction service's, as for the card.

**Stop conditions: NOT met.** One additive core function (the no-outcome case); no schema, DB_STORES, CSP, `_headers` or sanitiser change; the draft is written into no store or index.
REVIEW REQUIRED: (1) the preview draws with `EquationScheme` (the card's full-equation component, all reactants) and not the card's carried-substrate scheme, which lives in the navigator feature; "equals the card's scheme" in the tests means equals the `FullEquation` of the card's group (`group.equation`) for the demo. (2) One optional additive port field on `EditorPort` (not a core contract).

## Step 6.4a

### Step 6.4a, part 1 - fact sheet (2026-10-20)

No product code. Part A is commits de74f0f (review recorded) and e4537db (preview drawings asserted). **Stop condition: NOT met.** Every enum is closed and every number is a finite JS number; no unit or word list is open-ended, so no chemistry decision is missing.

**ConditionParameters** (`core/schema/conditions.ts:76-92`, strict object). Temperature / pressure / time are discriminated unions on `kind`:
- `temperature` (optional): `value {value: finite, unit}` | `range {min, max: finite, unit}` | `qualitative {value}`; unit `TEMPERATURE_UNITS` = C, K (:9); qualitative `QUALITATIVE_TEMPERATURES` = low_temperature, cold, room_temperature, warm, heat, reflux, strong_heat (:10-18). "Reflux" is a temperature word.
- `pressure` (optional, :33-42): value / range with `PRESSURE_UNITS` atm, bar, kPa, mmHg (:32); qualitative reduced | atmospheric | high. `time` (optional, :45-48): value with `TIME_UNITS` s, min, h, d (:44) | qualitative brief | prolonged; NO range.
- `medium` optional enum `MEDIA` acidic, basic, neutral, buffered (:50). `light` optional `LIGHT_CONDITIONS` dark, diffuse, uv, visible, sunlight, hv (:60). `atmosphere` optional `ATMOSPHERES` air, inert, nitrogen, argon, oxygen, hydrogen (:61). `anhydrous` optional boolean (three states: absent, true, false).
- `solventCharacter`: REQUIRED array of `SOLVENT_CHARACTERS` (aqueous, alcoholic, ethereal, polar_protic, polar_aprotic, non_polar, neat; :51-59), max 7 (the schema does not forbid a repeat). `activation`: REQUIRED array of `ACTIVATIONS` (electrolysis, ultrasound, microwave, radiation; :62), max 4. "Not stated" for an array is the empty array.
- `other`: REQUIRED array of `LabelTextSchema` (non-blank, single line, <= 200 chars, `primitives.ts:60`, LIMITS.label :12), max 16. `text`: optional `ShortTextSchema` (<= 2,000 chars, multi-line allowed). `parsedFields`: REQUIRED array of `PARAMETER_FIELDS` (:64-74: the nine structured fields above, not other/text), max 9.
- Numbers: `FiniteNumberSchema` (`primitives.ts:93`): any finite number, no limits. RXN-014 (`validation/rules/conditions.ts:28-60`, ERROR) flags a range with min > max, a temperature below absolute zero (C < -273.15, K < 0) and a pressure range min > max; the editor shows these as live findings and does not prevent them. A number is stored as a JS number, so "25.0" is stored 25 ("exactly as entered" holds for the value, not for trailing zeros).

**Stage** (`core/schema/reaction.ts:90-98`): `id`, `kind` (reaction | workup | quench | activation | purification), optional `label`, `participantIds`, `parameters: ConditionParameters`, optional `originalText`. Max 16 stages (`LIMITS.stages`). The editor's `addStage` (`workbench/stage-model.ts:31-35`) already creates the four empty arrays.
**ConditionVariant** (`reaction.ts:102-113`): `id`, `label` (REQUIRED, non-blank, <= 200), optional `stageId` (absent = "the first stage of kind reaction", the comment at :105 and the arrow builder `arrow-text.ts:159`), `parameters` (a full ConditionParameters; fields present override the stage's), `participantIds` (not edited in 6.4a), optional `note`. Max 16. The editor's `stageUseOf` (`stage-model.ts:68-78`) refuses removing a stage a variant names. I found no validation rule that checks a variant's `stageId` exists.
**What "overrides" means** (`condition-text.ts:98-113`, `overrideParameters`): temperature, pressure, time, medium, anhydrous, light, atmosphere and text override when PRESENT; `activation` and `other` override when non-empty. **`solventCharacter` and `parsedFields` are never merged**, so a variant's solventCharacter has no effect on the arrow (the arrow never writes solvent anyway). An empty array and "absent" are the same.

**parsedFields and RXN-015.** RXN-015 (`validation/rules/conditions.ts:68-83`, REVIEW_REQUIRED, L3) fires once per ParameterSet (every stage's parameters, every variant's parameters, reagent profiles, caveat triggers; :15-27) whose `parsedFields` is non-empty, path `...parameters.parsedFields`, data `{ fields }`. So it stops firing exactly when the list is empty. It does not look at the reaction's own `review`. The legacy importer (`io/legacy-v6/condition-parser.ts:96-135`) adds temperature, light, anhydrous, pressure, medium, solventCharacter and atmosphere (never time or activation). A field in parsedFields whose value was cleared stays listed unless the editor removes it (proposed: clearing a value removes it from parsedFields too).

**Text builder.** `conditionPartsOf(parameters)` (`core/graph/condition-text.ts:75-96`, exported by `core/graph/index.ts:20`) is PURE over a `ConditionParameters` value: it reads no state, so it can be called on a draft stage or variant (a value that fails the schema, e.g. a half-typed number, must be filtered by the form first). Order: temperature, pressure, light, medium, time, activation, atmosphere (a gas is a formula part), anhydrous (true only), other; `text` only when nothing structured gave a part (first line, 48 chars, ellipsis). Wording: "413 K", "25 °C", "0–5 °C" (en dash), "−10 to 5 °C", "room temperature", "acidic medium", "reduced pressure", "hν". **Not written: `solventCharacter`, `parsedFields`, `anhydrous: false`, stage label / kind / originalText.** The arrow applies a variant only when the arrow's outcome group names EXACTLY ONE variant (`arrow-text.ts:153-162`); then the variant's fields are laid over the stage it names. `previewOfDraft` already uses these builders, so the preview's arrows follow variants as the card does with no change.
**What outcomes reference:** `Outcome.conditionVariantIds` (`reaction.ts:157`, max 16; empty = all variants). RXN-020 (`reactions-more.ts:130-148`, WARNING) says a condition variant is not used by any outcome when there are 2+ variants and no outcome is for all variants: so a new variant no outcome names will show that warning until 6.4b.

**Demo data** (`data/seed/demo.orn.json`, 27 reactions; counted by script): 22 have stages, 21 have at least one structured stage field (medium 15, solventCharacter 14, temperature 11, anhydrous 5, atmosphere 1, pressure 1, light 1, other 1); **NO demo reaction has parsedFields**; exactly two have variants:
- `rxn_ethanol-conc-h2so4` (1 stage): `cvr_ethanol-conc-h2so4-1` "413 K, excess ethanol" (temperature 413 K) and `-2` "443 K, excess acid" (temperature 443 K), no `stageId` (default stage); outcomes name `[-1]` and `[-2]`.
- `rxn_ethanal-aldol` (0 STAGES): `cvr_ethanal-aldol-1` "Base-catalysed (dilute NaOH, cold)" (qualitative cold, basic medium, aqueous) and `-2` "Acid-catalysed" (acidic medium, aqueous); outcomes name them; no stageId.
Legacy: importing `data/fixtures/legacy/v6-demo-export.json` produces reactions with parsedFields (adv-043 test; `rxn_v6-r3` has 443 K), 32 RXN-015 rows in `legacy-expected/v6-demo-export.demo.preview.json`; `v4-sample.json` produces 9.

**Departures between the prompt and the code (REVIEW REQUIRED):**
(1) The demo's variant labels are "413 K, excess ethanol" / "443 K, excess acid", not "443 K"; the e2e changes the OVERRIDE (temperature 443 K to 453 K) and the summary line reads "443 K, excess acid: stage 1 temperature 443 K" (stage 1 = the default stage the variant does not name). (2) The summary line of a stage uses the arrow's builder, which does not write solventCharacter, anhydrous false or parsedFields: a stage with only those has an EMPTY builder line. Proposed: the line says "No conditions on the arrow" then; the rest is in the expanded form only. (3) The aldol reaction has variants but no stage, so a variant has nothing to override: its summary says "no stage to override" and the override picker is empty until a stage exists. (4) `solventCharacter` is editable in a variant but has no effect on the arrow or any other builder (said in the form's hint).

### Step 6.4a, part 2 - stage conditions and parsed fields (2026-10-20)

D1, D2, D4 built; no schema, DB_STORES, CSP, `_headers` or sanitiser change. Tests first (the model and component tests were written against the recipes and view before the form). Speed check 0.533 / 0.539 / 0.553 s (median 0.539 s): nothing deferred.
- **Model** (`condition-model.ts`, recipes over the draft, no chemistry): `setMeasureKind` / `setMeasureNumber` / `setMeasureChoice` (temperature, pressure, time), `setChoice` (medium, light, atmosphere), `setAnhydrous` (yes / no / Not stated; "no" is a stated `false`), `setListMember` (solvent character, activation; never twice), `setConditionText`, the qualifier list recipes, `confirmField`, `clearField`. A new measure stores ONLY its kind (the number, unit or word is then a schema finding, never a default); a value keeps its unit when it becomes a range; numbers are stored as typed (an emptied box removes the number, never 0 or NaN); every edit or clearing of a field also removes it from `parsedFields` (D2).
- **Summary** (`summaryOf`): `conditionPartsOf` (the arrow's builder, `core/graph/condition-text.ts`) over the parameters that already satisfy the schema (a half-typed value is left out), joined by " · "; nothing writable says "No conditions on the arrow" (REVIEW REQUIRED 1).
- **Form** (`condition-fields.tsx`, `condition-measure.tsx`, `condition.module.css`): its own component, reused by the variants in part 3 through `only` (the fields drawn) and `onRemove`. Every enum list comes from the schema's own constants (units, qualitative words, media, light, atmosphere, solvent character, activation). - REQUIRED: `id` (OutcomeId, prefix `out`, references.ts:275), `conditionVariantIds` (array of ConditionVariantId, max 16, empty = all variants), `selectivity`, `products` (max `LIMITS.products` = 32), `conceptIds` (max `LIMITS.idList` = 256; the editor leaves it as it is).
- `selectivity`: enum `SELECTIVITIES` (reaction.ts:115) = exclusive, major, minor, trace, mixture_component, unspecified. "unspecified" is a valid value, so a new outcome can start there.

- Text types (primitives.ts:60-80): LabelText = one line, max 200, not blank, no control/bidi characters; ShortText = multi-line, max 2,000; RichText = ORN mini-markup string, max 50,000 (rich-text.ts:31-34 lists `outcomes[].rationale`, `.note`, `.products[].note`, `.stereochemistry.note`). `rationale` is RichText. An empty LabelText is refused (not blank), so "cleared" must remove the field.
**Product** (reaction.ts:131): REQUIRED `id` (prefix `pdt`), `ref` (`SpeciesOrClassRefSchema`, refs.ts:18: `{kind:'species'|'class', id}`; NOT a reagent), `role` enum `PRODUCT_ROLES` (reaction.ts:116) = main, coproduct, byproduct. OPTIONAL `coefficient` (PositiveNumber), `phase` (PHASES = s, l, g, aq, alc, soln, melt), `originalText` (ShortText), `note` (RichText). Delete rule for `products[].ref`: restrict (references.ts:157).
**Stereochemistry** (reaction.ts:142): `{ outcome (REQUIRED, enum STEREO_OUTCOMES, reaction.ts:117: retention, inversion, racemisation, syn_addition, anti_addition, cis_selective, trans_selective, enantiomeric_pair, diastereomeric_mixture, no_new_stereocentre, unspecified), descriptors (REQUIRED array of LabelText, max 16, e.g. "Z"), note? (RichText) }`. The whole field is optional.
**Mechanism link** (reaction.ts:148): `{ mechanismId, variantId? }`; references.ts:160-167 (mechanism and its variant). Read-only in 6.4b.
**Rules** (VALIDATION_RULES §2, rules/reactions.ts): RXN-002 no outcome with a product (path `outcomes`); RXN-003 an outcome with zero products (path `outcomes[i].products`; draft WARNING / published ERROR via `lifecycleSeverity`, helpers.ts:24); RXN-008 exclusive overlapping (path `outcomes[i].selectivity`, ERROR; empty variant list = all); RXN-009 minor without major (path `outcomes[i].selectivity`, WARNING). So the marker for an outcome is its index in the path. Note: D2 says RXN-003 without a severity; it is WARNING while the reaction is a draft and ERROR once Published (the Review section's gate, D5).
**What scope allows a product to be.** The SCHEMA allows species or class for every reaction; NO rule or schema field ties scope to product kind (grep of `src/core` finds none). The convention (DOMAIN_MODEL §6, line 177): generic reactions are written with classes, specific with concrete species. The demo follows it for products (generic: 1 class product; specific: 47 species products, 0 classes); for participants one generic reaction has a species and a reagent, so participants are not held to it. DECISION TAKEN for the picker (a UI limit, no chemistry): a specific reaction offers species, a generic one offers classes, a reaction with no scope yet offers both with a hint "Choose a scope"; a product already stored of the other kind stays shown and editable. Marked REVIEW REQUIRED.
**Where a reaction appears** (GRAPH_SEMANTICS §3 lines 37-42; `navigator-rollup.ts:140-156`; `family/study.ts:99`): the carried substrate is the participant flagged `isPrimarySubstrate`, else the FIRST reactant (spectators and never-a-node species skipped); the arrows go to the hub of each product whose role is `main` (and that is drawn as a node). The hub of a substance is the anchored class it is classified in, else the nearest anchored ancestor class (`classIds` then parents), else Unclassified. The family page "Reactions of <family>" is built from `candidatesFrom(hub)`, grouped by the TARGET hub, headed "To <hub name>" (the existing test: navigator-family.test.tsx:53 `To Aldehydes`). The demo anchors Alcohols (`anc_alcohols`, class `cls_alcohols`) and Aldehydes (`anc_aldehydes`, `cls_aldehydes`). A new Propan-1-ol with class Alcohols and Propanal with class Aldehydes: the reaction appears on the Alcohols family page, section "Reactions of Alcohols", group "To Aldehydes", and on Aldehydes under "Preparations" ("From Alcohols").
**Demo content for the e2e:** the demo has NO propan-1-ol and NO propanal; it HAS Dichloromethane (`spc_dichloromethane`, no classes), a PCC reagent (`rgt_pcc`) and species `spc_pcc`, and the reaction "1° alcohol → aldehyde (PCC)" (`rxn_alcohol1-to-aldehyde-pcc`), so the new reaction's card has two relatives in the same group. The from-scratch e2e creates both species.
No stop condition reached: no field needs a chemistry decision beyond the one flagged above (the picker limit, a UI choice with the schema unchanged). ### Step 6.5a, part A - 6.4 close recorded and follow-ups (2026-10-20)

**Toasts.** `ToastProvider` takes optional injected `timers` (`ToastTimers`: `set`, `clear`; real timers by default). A toast with `autoDismissMs` closes after that time; the countdown stops while the pointer is over the toast or focus is inside it and starts again (full time) when both end. `RESULT_TOAST_MS = 6000` (primitives) is now used by the editor host for "Saved", "Saved, N warnings", "Draft kept", "Draft discarded". Toasts with an action ("Undo import") and every toast pushed without `autoDismissMs` (errors, "Structure duplicates could not be checked", refusals) stay until dismissed. The live region still announces each addition once; the save state stays in the status line. Note: "Saved, N warnings" is a warning-kind toast but is in the prompt's explicit auto-close list, so it closes too (the warnings stay in the findings). The import results toast keeps its own 20 s (`data-exchange` `RESULT_TOAST_MS`, a different constant with the same name; unchanged). ### Step 6.5a, part 1 - fact sheet (2026-10-20)

No product code. Everything below was read from the files named.

**Mechanism** (`src/core/schema/mechanism.ts:108-121`, strict object): `id` (mec_), `kind: 'mechanism'`, `name` NameText (<= 300, one line), `aliases` NameText[] (<= 64, `primitives.ts:19`), `mechanismClasses` Classification[] (<= 16; `{conceptId, certainty: definite|probable|possible}`), `summary?` RichText (<= 50,000), `variants` (<= 16, `primitives.ts:30`), `conceptIds` (<= 256), `studyNotes?` RichText, `notes?` RichText, then `recordMetaShape` (`primitives.ts:209`): `tags` (<= 64), `citations` (<= 64), `provenance` (`origin` user|seed|import|legacy_import|generated, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, optional `importBatchId`, `legacy`), `review` (`lifecycle` draft|published, `status` unreviewed|review_required|verified, optional `confidence`, `reasons` ShortText[], optional `reviewedAt`). It has NO `names` object: a flat `name` + `aliases`, like a reaction. Required: id, kind, name, aliases, mechanismClasses, variants, conceptIds, tags, citations, provenance, review.
**Variant** (`mechanism.ts:97-106`): `id` (mvr_), `label` LabelText (<= 200, required), `applicability?` RichText, `steps` (<= 200, `primitives.ts:31`), `rateLaw?` LabelText, `note?` RichText.
**Step** (`:82-95`): `id` (mst_), `title?` LabelText, `stepKinds` array of the 18 values (bond_formation, bond_cleavage, proton_transfer, nucleophilic_attack, electrophilic_attack, leaving_group_departure, rearrangement, hydride_shift, alkyl_shift, radical_initiation, radical_propagation, radical_termination, tautomerisation, addition, elimination, electron_transfer, coordination, other; `:19-38`; required, may be empty), `description?` RichText, `species` (<= 24, `primitives.ts:32`), `bondsFormed` / `bondsBroken` / `electronMovements` (each <= 64, `primitives.ts:33`), `isRateDetermining?`, `reversible?` booleans, `stereochemicalEvent?` LabelText, `note?` RichText.
**Step species** (`:75-80`): `role` of 7 (reactant, reagent, intermediate, transition_state, product, leaving_group, catalyst; `:40-48`), optional `ref` (SubstanceRef: species | class | reagent, `refs.ts:10`), `label?` LabelText, `structure?` StructureRep (`primitives.ts:197`: `format` smiles|cxsmiles|molfile, `value` 1..1,000,000 chars; line notations <= 20,000). At least one of ref / label / structure (MEC-002).
**Bond change** (`:53-58`): `atoms` a tuple of two atom maps, `order?` 1|2|3, `aromatic?` boolean, `note?` LabelText. **Atom map** (`:51`): integer 1..999.
**Electron movement** (`:68-72`): `from`, `to` (sites), `electrons` 1 | 2 (required).
**Site shape** (`:60-65`, discriminated on `kind`): `{kind:'atom', atom}`, `{kind:'lone_pair', atom}`, `{kind:'radical', atom}`, `{kind:'bond', atoms:[a,b]}`. No charge site. The demo uses lone_pair>bond (7), bond>bond (5), bond>lone_pair (7).
**Rules.** MEC-001 INFO (no variants, or a variant with no steps), MEC-002 ERROR (step species with none of ref/label/structure), MEC-003 WARNING (electron movements and no step structure with atom maps; a molfile counts as possibly mapped), MEC-004 WARNING (more than one rate-determining step in a variant): `src/core/validation/rules/mechanisms.ts:26,46,69,93`. CHEM-008 WARNING is L4 (`rules/external.ts:16`): `src/chem/checks/plan-mechanism.ts` builds one request per step that has bond changes or arrows (paths `variants[i].steps[j].bondsFormed[k]` / `bondsBroken[k]` / `electronMovements[k]`; a step with uses but no structure is "not compared"); `src/chem/checks/mechanism.ts:9-36` compares each use's maps with the maps RDKit reads from the step's structures (hydrogens that carry a map counted, `rdkit/mapped-hydrogens.ts`) and yields "Atom map N is not on any atom of the structures of this step" at the row's path. REF-008 WARNING (`rules/references.ts:110`, paths from `RICH_TEXT_PATHS`, `schema/rich-text.ts:9`; for a mechanism: notes, studyNotes, summary, variants[].applicability, variants[].note, variants[].steps[].description, variants[].steps[].note) for a [[link]] to a missing record.
**Atom maps in the chem worker today.** `ChemService.parse(structure)` returns `facts.atomMaps` (ascending, repeats kept; `chem/contracts.ts:36`, `rdkit/facts.ts:146`, with mapped hydrogens from `adapter.ts:124`) and the editor already holds it as `StructurePort.parse` (`workbench/structure-contracts.ts`). So LISTING the maps needs NO new worker method. The BONDS between mapped atoms are not in the facts (MinimalLib's JSON has no map numbers; `smiles-atoms.ts` reads atoms only). Reading for D4 (a REVIEW REQUIRED item): atom / lone-pair / radical sites are chosen from the step's maps; a bond site (and a bond change) from PAIRS of the step's maps, lower number first; a pair is not filtered by whether the atoms are bonded, because that needs a bond reader the worker does not have. CHEM-008 still checks every map.
**Links.** `reaction.mechanismIds` (`reaction.ts:232`): MechanismId[] <= 16, required array; registry row `references.ts:174`, delete policy detach. `outcome.mechanism` (`reaction.ts:148-151,166`): optional `{mechanismId, variantId?}`; registry rows `references.ts:158-170` (`mechanismId` detach with container `outcomes[].mechanism`; `variantId` a nested reference to the sibling mechanism's variants, detach). NO rule requires an outcome's mechanism to be in the reaction's `mechanismIds`; the D5 editor enforces it. Graph: `core/graph/mechanisms/build.ts:34` uses `mechanismIds`; `core/graph/related/related.ts:127` reads both.
**Rich text.** `RichText` = string <= 50,000 (`primitives.ts:78`), validated, never transformed. `core/text`: `parseRichText(source): RichNode[]` (total; malformed degrades to literal text), `richTextLinks(source): RecordRef[]`, `rewriteRichTextLinks`, `richTextParser` (`text/richtext.ts:232,241,272,278`); AST `RichNode` = text | strong | em | sub | sup | link{target,label} | paragraph | bullets (`text/contracts.ts`). Markup per DOMAIN_MODEL 3.4: `*em*`, `**strong**`, `_{sub}`, `^{sup}`, `- ` bullets, blank line = paragraph, `[[rxn_...|label]]`. The only React renderer is in `features/inspector/rich-text.tsx`, which needs the inspector's environment; features may not import each other, so Part 2 writes its own small renderer in the workbench (same AST, text as React children only).
**New mechanism.** `core/editing/blank.ts` has no mechanism case (it returns undefined; `openSession` would start `{kind, id}`). Part 3 adds `{kind:'mechanism', id, name:'', aliases:[], mechanismClasses:[], variants:[], conceptIds:[], tags:[], citations:[], provenance:{origin:'user', createdAt, updatedAt}, review:{lifecycle:'draft', status:'unreviewed', reasons:[]}}` (the same `startMeta` as the other kinds; the empty name fails L1 until typed, as for a reaction).
**Demo mechanisms (`data/seed/demo.orn.json`):** 3, all published, review_required, origin seed: `mec_aldol-ethanal` (2 variants: base 3 steps, acid 4 steps; base steps 1-3 and acid step 3 have atom-mapped structures, acid steps 1, 2 and 4 have none), `mec_e2-haloalkane` (2 variants, 1 step each, all mapped, 2 bonds formed, 2 broken, 3 movements, a description), `mec_sn2-haloalkane` (1 variant, 1 mapped step with `title` and `stereochemicalEvent`). Variants have applicability and rateLaw (E2, SN2 variants). Linked by `rxn_ethanal-aldol`, `rxn_r-2-bromobutane-alc-koh`, `rxn_r-2-bromobutane-aq-koh` (each reaction's `mechanismIds` and its outcomes' `mechanism.variantId`; 5 outcome links in all).

### Step 6.5b, part 1 - pictures fact sheet (2026-10-20)

No product code (docs only: the 6.5b decisions P1-P8 are added to ADR-038 and ADR-040's addenda, UI_ARCHITECTURE §7 and §9). Everything below was read from the files named.
**Asset record** (`src/core/schema/assets.ts:23-41`, strict object): `id` (ast_), `kind: 'asset'`, `mediaType` enum `image/png | image/jpeg | image/webp | image/gif | image/svg+xml` (`:12`), `byteSize` int 1..`MAX_ASSET_BYTES` = 20 MiB (`:21`, required), `sha256` 64 lowercase hex (required), `width?` / `height?` int 1..32,768, `filename?` LabelText (<= 200, not blank; "sanitised base name only; never a path"), `altText?` ShortText (<= 2,000, one line: no control or bidi characters), `assetRole` enum of 6 (`structure_image, reaction_image, mechanism_image, reagent_image, reference_image, legacy_image`; required), `attachedTo` array (<= 64, `LIMITS.attachments`) of `{ref: RecordRef, note?: ShortText}` (required), `caption?` RichText (<= 50,000), then `recordMetaShape` (tags, citations, provenance, review: required, as every record). No required field needs a choice or a content decision: the role for a mechanism picture is `mechanism_image`; the rest is the file's own facts. Alt text is OPTIONAL in the schema; the dialog requires it (P2).
**How an asset is attached.** The ASSET holds the link: `attachedTo[].ref` (a `RecordRef` {kind, id}; ID prefix must match the kind, `refs.ts:25-27`), registry row `references.ts:222-229` (target kinds up to layer 3, so a mechanism is allowed; delete policy `detach`, container `attachedTo[]`). The mechanism record has NO field for assets. So the pattern is P3 (a): the mechanism record is not changed and its open draft is not touched. A `RecordRef` names a record, never a place inside one, so it CANNOT name a mechanism STEP without a schema change: mechanism pictures only, and the openItem "-> later: pictures on a single mechanism step need a schema change (asset attachment to a step)" is added (the prompt's P1 fallback; not a stop).
**AST rules / INV-17.** AST-001 INFO "Asset attached to nothing" (`core/validation/rules/curriculum.ts:225-236`: `attachedTo` empty AND no referrers, e.g. no scheme uses it; so a detached picture is reported as today); AST-002 WARNING blob missing and AST-003 ERROR hash mismatch are raised by persistence and import (`rules/external.ts:7-8`, VALIDATION_RULES.md:126-128, :164). INV-17 (`ARCHITECTURE.md:155`): assets are optional, no chemistry exists only as an image, deleting an asset never invalidates chemistry (nothing a picture does touches chemistry fields).
**Media types, magic bytes, cap.** `io/asset-magic.ts` `magicBytesMatch(bytes, mediaType)`: PNG 8-byte signature, JPEG `FF D8 FF`, GIF87a/89a, WebP `RIFF....WEBP`, SVG a text sniff of the first 4 kB (`<?xml`, `<svg`, `<!doctype svg`); any other declared type is false. Cap `IMPORT_LIMITS.maxAssetBytes` = 20 MiB (`io/contracts.ts:14`; SECURITY.md §3 "Asset 20 MB, magic bytes must match media type, SHA-256 verified"). `ASSET_MEDIA_TYPES` is the `accept` list. The browser's own file type is not trusted: the dialog sniffs the bytes and takes the media type from the match (a .png that is really something else is refused).
**SHA-256 and blobs today.** `io/hash.ts` `sha256Hex(bytes)` (`crypto.subtle`). Only IMPORT carries blobs today: `AssetStagePort.stage / clear` (`io/import-ports.ts:49-56`), the app's `createAssetStage()` (`app/services/flow-ports.ts:19-41`) whose `blobsFor(changes)` returns the staged bytes of the asset records the ChangeSet creates or updates, wired as `createWriterPart({blobsFor})` (`app/services/create.ts:98-99`, `writer.ts:32,99`, `persistence/write-wiring.ts:18,37`) into `adapter.writeChanges(changes, next, blobs?)` (`persistence/contracts.ts:250`); `coalesce.ts:37-47` refuses a blob without a created/updated asset record or with a different hash; `adapter.ts:128-134` adds the rows only if no row with that hash exists, in the one transaction with the records (INV-20; PERSISTENCE §5: rows are never overwritten or deleted). The editor's save path does NOT pass blobs: drafts commit through `drafts.commit` -> `store.dispatch` with no stage. Also `createAssetStage` is not exposed on `AppServices`. Smallest additive change (listed under Amendments below): ONE additive port `AppServices.pictures` (`add`, `edit`, `detach`; implemented in a lazy module over the existing asset stage, `ids`, and `store.dispatch`, so a picture is `stage(bytes)` -> `dispatch({commands: [record.create asset]})` -> `clear()`; the store notifies the write queue synchronously, as `replaceState` does for import). No schema, DB_STORES or persistence contract change.
**Global Undo / Redo.** `store.undo()/redo()` (`core/commands/store.ts:183-197`) apply the entry's inverse patches / patches through the same commit step: undoing the add yields a ChangeSet that DELETES the asset record; the blob row stays (never deleted, PERSISTENCE §5.2) and is reused by hash if the same file is added again; Redo re-creates the record with no staged bytes, which is fine because the row exists (and `checkBlobs` only runs when blobs are passed). History is cleared by a reload (as for every edit).
**Inspector.** `app/window/inspector-port.ts:20-33` is the assets port (`open(assetId, mediaType)` reads `persistence.getAssetBlob(assetId)`, which finds the record's sha256 then the blob row, and returns `URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([blob], {type}))`; `revoke`); `features/inspector/contracts.ts:41-44` its type; `view-asset.tsx` `AssetImageView` makes the URL in an effect and revokes it on cleanup, with "loading" and a "none" state in words (missing: "The bytes of this image are not stored (finding AST-002)."), `<img>` only. The mechanism view is `features/inspector/view-mechanism.tsx` (`MechanismLevels`), in the lazy `views-other` chunk (`lazy-views.tsx`, `views-other.tsx:35`).
**Stop conditions: none met** (no required field needs a decision; saving a picture needs no schema or DB_STORES change; the save path needs ONE additive port).
**Amendments.** (1) `AppServices.pictures`, a new additive member (`app/services/contracts.ts`), see above; docs updated in this commit (ADR-038 addendum). (2) openItem "-> later: pictures on a single mechanism step need a schema change (asset attachment to a step)".

### Studio step, part 2 - the two editions (2026-10-20)

E1, E2, E3 (build side only; nothing deployed). Tests written first and seen RED (missing modules / missing script) before the code: `src/app/edition.test.ts` (5), `editor-commands.test.ts` (2), `edition-window.test.tsx` (6: both editions loaded once each at collection, each with its own module registry), `shell.test.tsx` (+2, the marker), `editor-services-inert.test.ts` (5), `tests/integration/check-edition.test.ts` (7: passes both fixtures, FAILS a Study fixture with an editor module in a lazy chunk or ONE in the entry chunk, FAILS a Studio fixture with none, a report for the wrong edition / missing / not a report, the 395 kB line).
**The constant.** `src/app/edition.ts`: `EDITION` ('study' | 'studio'), `EDITING`, `STUDIO_NAME = 'Studio'` (the ONE place the word lives), `SITE_TITLE`, `pageTitleOf()` ("ORN Studio" / "Organic Reaction Navigator"), `editionMarker()`. The literal is `__ORN_EDITION__` (`vite.config.ts` `define`, declared in `globals.d.ts`); anything but exactly 'studio' is Study. `vite.config.ts` reads `ORN_EDITION` (`scripts/edition.mjs <study|studio> <vite args>` sets it: no shell syntax); no value = Study, except under Vitest = Studio (every existing editor test is unchanged); another value stops the build. Outputs: `dist` (Study) and `dist-studio` (Studio, git-ignored; eslint ignores it, with `build-report/`).
**The guards (entry points only; no core file changed).** `window.tsx`: `EditorsProvider`, the Workbench page, the palette's editing deps (`editor-commands.ts`, which now holds `editNamesCommand` and the five New commands, `{}` in Study), `HistoryKeys` and the `history` of the top bar and the phone bar (so no Undo / Redo on the bar, in More or on the keys), all behind `EDITING`; `modes.ts` lists Workbench only when `EDITING`; `phone-parts.tsx` More's Workbench section only when `EDITING`; `drafts-ui.tsx` `useDraftsView()` is the empty view in Study (no start-up drafts line, no Drafts menu item: drafts already stored in a visitor's browser are neither read nor touched); `create.ts` builds the real draft manager and the two lazy checks only when `EDITING`, otherwise `editor-services-inert.ts` (same shapes; nothing read or written); `top-bar.tsx` `history` is now optional. `shell.tsx` takes `marker`; the window passes `editionMarker()`: a bordered word beside the title on desktop and phone ("Studio"), outside the `h1`. `main.tsx` sets `document.title = pageTitleOf()` at start-up (no `<title>` change in `index.html`: the static title stays the public one).
**What it took to make the bundler drop the modules (found by running the check, not guessed).** (1) `lazy()` calls at the top of `editors.tsx` kept their `import()` calls (a module-level call counts as a side effect): `/* @__PURE__ */`. (2) Importing `hasNames` from the `@/core/editing` barrel executes the barrel's modules (`session.ts` calls `enablePatches()`, `stored.ts` builds zod schemas): `inspector.tsx` now imports `@/core/editing/names` directly (dependency rules still pass). (3) Any chain to the barrel from a module that is in the graph keeps those side effects, so `vite.config.ts` sets `treeshake.moduleSideEffects` to false for the editor modules in the Study build only. If a Study entry point ever used one of them, its code would stay in the bundle and the check below would fail the build.
**The proof (E2).** The Vite manifest has no module list (Part 1), so `vite.config.ts` has a small plugin (`orn-module-report`, also in the worker builds) that writes every chunk's modules that put code in it to `build-report/<edition>.json`. `scripts/editor-modules.json` is the ONE list of editor modules (prefixes and exact paths; read by the config and by the check; not listed on purpose: `core/editing/names.ts`, schema knowledge the inspector reads, and `drafts-ui.tsx`, the React context). `scripts/check-edition.mjs <edition> [dist] [report]`: Study: none in ANY chunk (entry, lazy, workers); Studio: at least one; the report must be for that edition; the initial JS gzip is reported; Studio is held to 395 kB. REVIEW REQUIRED: the module list comes from the build's own report, not from "the manifest's module list" (the manifest has none); and `names.ts` / `drafts-ui.tsx` are not on the list.
**Result** (`npm run build:smoke`, both editions, one command; Study: `check-build` against `dist`, `check-edition study`; then Studio against `dist-studio`): Study 14 chunks, **0 editor modules**, initial JS **386.19 kB gzip**; Studio 19 chunks, 106 editor modules, initial JS **391.99 kB gzip** (the 395 kB line holds; Part 1's last figure was 391.32 kB, +0.67 kB for `edition.ts`, the inert services, `editor-commands.ts` and the marker). Before the three fixes above the check failed with 97 modules in the Study build: it does fail on a wrong build.
**E3.** `wrangler.studio.jsonc` (name `reaction-navigator-studio`, assets `./dist-studio`, static only, same `compatibility_date`); `wrangler.jsonc` stays the Study Worker (`reaction-navigator`, `./dist`). ### Studio step, part 4 - publishing (2026-10-20)

E4 built. Nothing is published for real: `data/published/` does not exist in the repo (the test fixtures are made through the export builders; one manual run published `data/seed/demo.orn.json` to prove the build and the folder was deleted again).
**The check and the script.** `src/io/publish.ts` `checkForPublish(file, {store (an EMPTY dataset), ids, runner})` runs the same pipeline as the app (`parseImportSource`, then a `replace_all` preview: envelope, migrations, L1 per record, L1-L3 over the merged result, assets with magic bytes and SHA-256) and refuses, in words, on: a file the parser rejects; an older-app (legacy) file; a record the file lists that fails L1; a preview that cannot be confirmed (its blockers); any ERROR finding; a rejected asset; a package entry that could not be read; picture records with no bytes (REVIEW REQUIRED: this last refusal and the legacy refusal go beyond "L1 ERROR or rejected asset"; a published picture must show to everyone and a legacy file is imported in Studio first). `scripts/publish-dataset.mjs` (`npm run publish:dataset -- <file>`; `tsx`'s `register` gives it the repo's TypeScript and `@/` paths in Node) reads the file, runs the check, prints the record counts, the finding summary and up to 20 findings, then writes `data/published/dataset.orn.json` (or `dataset.ornpkg`, named by the checked format; the other is removed) and `manifest.json` (`manifestVersion`, `file`, `format`, `sha256`, `bytes`, `publishedAt` from the injected clock `ORN_NOW`, `recordTotal`, `recordCounts`), each written beside and renamed, so a refusal or a crash leaves the old dataset exactly as it was. Exit 0 accepted, 1 refused (missing file included), 2 usage. `ORN_PUBLISH_DIR` changes the folder (the tests).
**Shipping it.** `vite.config.ts` `datasetModule` (`virtual:orn-dataset`): Study with `data/published/manifest.json` ships that file (hashed asset, with its sha256 and time) and NOT the demo; every other build ships the demo. `ORN_PUBLISHED_DIR` points the build at another folder (the e2e builds over a fixture). `main.tsx` fetches `dataset.url` with `dataset.fileName`. `check-build.mjs` rule 5 is edition-aware (`check-build.mjs <dist> <doc> <edition> [publishedDir]`, passed by `build:smoke`): Study with a published dataset must hold exactly one copy equal to the published file, a manifest whose sha256 is the file's, and no demo; otherwise the demo as before and no study dataset file. Run with a real published fixture: Study 14 chunks, 0 editor modules, initial JS 387.20 kB gzip, `study dataset: assets/dataset.orn-<hash>.json ... identical`, Studio 392.73 kB with the demo (the 395 kB line holds).
**In the window (Study only).** `dataset-types.ts` / `dataset-info.tsx` (`DatasetInfo` demo | published, `DatasetProvider`, `datasetWordsOf`, `studyUpdateDue`, `createDatasetInfo`): the sha256 last loaded is kept in `uiState` key `studyDataset` as `{ sha256 }` (no schema or DB_STORES change; read tolerantly at boot, written in a writer tab when a load of the published dataset is APPLIED: `ImportModel.openBlob(..., { onApplied })`, called once by the existing apply path, never on a refusal or a cancel). Load it (this replaces the data in this browser; export a backup first if you imported your own data)." with "Load it" (the existing replace import: `replace_all`, its pre-import snapshot, Undo import; the new sha256 is remembered and the notice goes) and "Later" (hidden for this visit; asked again at the next one). Due when the published sha256 differs from the one last loaded (a browser that never loaded one counts) AND the dataset has records (an empty one gets the first-run screen).
